Fifth Month of Midsummer
5.1 "Record of Midsummer"
First: In the month of Midsummer:
the sun is in Dongjing (the constellation Gemini),
at dusk, Kang (the constellation Virgo) is in the meridian,
at dawn, Wei (the constellation Aquarius) is in the meridian.
Its days are Bing and Ding.
Its Emperor is Yan Di (the Fire Emperor).
Its spirit is Zhurong (god of fire).
Its insect is feathered (birds).
Its musical note is Zhi.
The corresponding musical tube is Ruibin.
Its number is seven.
Its taste is bitter.
Its smell is scorched.
Its sacrifice is to the hearth (stove).
The offering comes first with the lungs.
Slight Heat arrives.
The praying mantis is born.
The shrike begins to sing.
The mockingbird is silent.
The Son of Heaven dwells in the Bright Hall Great Temple,
riding a vermillion carriage,
drawn by red-bay horses,
bearing a red banner,
Wearing scarlet robes,
adorning themselves with red jade,
eating beans and chicken.
Their vessels are tall and rough.
They raise strong, cunning creatures.
In this month,
they command the music masters
to repair the small drums and large drums,
to tune the zithers, lutes, pipes, and flutes,
to hold shields, axes, spears, and feathers,
to adjust the yu, sheng, xun, and chi,
to arrange the bells, chimes, zhu, and yu.
They order the officials
to pray to the mountains, rivers, and all the plains for the people,
to perform a grand rain dance to the Emperor,
using magnificent music.
Then they command all the counties
to perform rain sacrifices to all the lords and officials who have benefited the people,
in order to pray for grain to ripen.
Then the farmers present millet.
In this month,
the Son of Heaven tastes the new millet with young fowl,
presenting it with cherries,
first offering it in the ancestral temple.
He orders the people not to cut indigo for dyeing,
not to burn charcoal,
not to expose cloth to the sun.
The gates and doors are not closed;
the barriers and markets make no demands.
Release serious prisoners
and increase their rations.
Separate the wandering female animals from their herds,
then tether up the leaping foals
and regulate the distribution of horses.
In this month,
the day reaches its longest.
Yin and Yang contend,
and death and life are divided.
The ruler fasts and purifies himself;
his dwelling must be secluded,
desiring stillness and no agitation,
ceasing sounds and colors,
with nothing allowed to advance,
with bland flavors,
and nothing to achieve harmony,
retreating from desires and lusts,
settling the heart and qi.
All officials are quiet;
affairs have no shortcuts,
in order to settle the establishment of the flourishing yin.
The deer antlers fall off.
The cicadas begin to sing.
*Pinellia ternata* (半夏) grows,
and the hibiscus (木堇) blooms.
In this month,
do not use fire in the southern direction.
One can reside in high and bright places,
one can gaze into the distance,
one can climb mountains and hills,
one can dwell in terraces and pavilions.
If in midsummer, winter commands are executed,
then hail and sleet will damage the grain,
roads will be impassable,
and violent soldiers will arrive.
If spring commands are executed,
then the five grains will mature late,
various pests will arise at the wrong time,
and the country will be hungry.
If autumn commands are executed,
then grasses and trees will wither,
fruits will ripen early,
and the people will suffer from plagues.
5.2 *Da Yue*
Secondly, the origin of music is distant,
arising from measure and standard,
rooted in the Great One (Taiyi).
The Great One produces the Two Forms (Liangyi),
the Two Forms produce Yin and Yang.
The changes of yin and yang,
one goes up and one goes down,
combining to form patterns.
Murky and chaotic,
separating then reuniting,
uniting then separating again,
this is called the constant of Heaven.
Heaven and earth are like cartwheels,
ending then beginning again,
reaching the extreme then reverting back,
without exception, all are appropriate.
The sun, moon, and stars,
sometimes fast, sometimes slow,
the sun and moon are different,
in order to complete their course.
The four seasons arise,
sometimes hot, sometimes cold,
sometimes short, sometimes long,
sometimes yielding, sometimes firm.
The myriad things come forth,
created by the Great One,
transformed by yin and yang.
Sprouts begin to stir,
condensing into forms.
Physical bodies have their places,
and all have sounds.
Sounds come from harmony,
harmony comes from appropriateness.
Harmony and accord: the former kings established music
arising from this.
When the world is at peace,
and all things are tranquil,
all are transformed by their superiors,
then music can be achieved.
To achieve music, there must be preparation;
one must restrain desires and passions.
If desires and passions are not avoided,
then music cannot be pursued.
Pursuing music has a method;
it must certainly originate from fairness.
Fairness comes from impartiality,
and impartiality comes from the Dao.
Therefore, only those who attain the Dao
are fit to discuss music!
States ruined and people slaughtered,
it is not that they have no music;
it is that their music is not true music.
A drowning man is not incapable of laughter,
a criminal is not incapable of song,
a madman is not incapable of dance;
the music of a chaotic age
is similar to these.
When rulers and ministers lose their positions,
fathers and sons lose their places,
husbands and wives lose their propriety,
The people groan in suffering,
yet they consider it a pleasure.
How can this be?
In general, music
is the harmony of Heaven and Earth,
the balance of yin and yang.
Heaven is what initially gives birth to people;
people have no part in it.
Heaven causes people to have desires;
people cannot but seek them.
Heaven causes people to have aversions;
people cannot but avoid them.
Desires and aversions are received from Heaven;
people cannot participate in them,
they cannot be changed,
they cannot be altered.
Among the scholars of the world,
there are those who disapprove of music.
How does this arise?
Great music
is what brings joy and delight to ruler and minister, father and son, elders and youngsters.
Joy and delight arise from peace,
and peace arises from the Way.
The Way
cannot be seen when looked at,
cannot be heard when listened to,
and cannot be given a form.
One who knows how to see the unseen,
To hear the unheard, to shape the shapeless,
then one is close to understanding.
The Dao,
is the utmost essence,
that cannot be formed,
that cannot be named;
forcing a name upon it, we call it the Great One.
Therefore, the One establishes commands,
the Two follows and listens.
The former sages chose to legislate with Two, but return to One,
and thereby understood the feelings of all things.
Therefore, one who can govern with the One,
brings joy to the ruler and ministers,
harmonizes those near and far,
pleases the common people,
and unites the relatives.
One who can govern oneself with the One,
avoids disaster,
completes one's life,
and fulfills one's Heaven-sent destiny.
One who can govern one's state with the One,
banishes the wicked,
attracts the virtuous,
and achieves great transformation.
One who can govern all under Heaven with the One,
makes cold and heat appropriate,
makes wind and rain timely,
and becomes a sage.
Therefore, to know one thing is to be enlightened;
to be enlightened by two things is to be deranged.
5.3 Extravagant Music
It is said: People all sustain their lives by living,
but they do not know the reason they live.
People all know through their knowledge,
but they do not know the reason they know.
Knowing the reason one knows is called understanding the Dao;
not knowing the reason one knows is called discarding treasure.
Those who discard treasure will certainly suffer misfortune.
The rulers of the world
mostly consider pearls, jade, halberds, and swords to be treasures.
The more treasures they have, the more resentful the people become;
the more endangered the country becomes;
the more precarious their personal situation becomes;
thus, they lose the true meaning of treasure.
The music of a chaotic age is similar to this.
When the sounds of wood and leather are like thunder,
when the sounds of metal and stone are like lightning,
when the sounds of stringed instruments, flutes, singing, and dancing are like clamor,
it may be possible to startle the mind,
move the ears and eyes,
and agitate life,
but if one considers this to be pleasure, then it is not pleasure.
Therefore, the more extravagant the music,
And the people become increasingly oppressed,
the country becomes increasingly chaotic,
the ruler becomes increasingly degraded;
then one also loses the true essence of joy.
Generally speaking, what the ancient sage kings valued in music
was its essence.
Xia Jie and Yin Zhou created extravagant music,
with sounds of large drums, bells, chimes, pipes, and flutes,
considering largeness as beauty,
and crowds as spectacle,
initiating bizarre and strange things,
that the ears had never heard,
that the eyes had never seen,
striving to surpass each other,
without using moderation.
When Song was declining,
they made "Thousand Bells."
When Qi was declining,
they made "Great Lü."
When Chu was declining,
they made "Witch Music."
Extravagant it was,
but when those who understand the Way observe it,
they lose the true essence of joy.
Losing the true essence of joy
makes joy not joyful.
If joy is not joyful,
the people will surely resent it,
and their lives will surely be harmed.
The relationship between their lives and joy
is like ice exposed to the blazing sun or charcoal,
which turns back to injure itself.
This arises from not understanding the essence of joy.
Generally, music is connected to governance and influences customs.
When customs are settled, music transforms them.
Customs are settled and music transforms them.
Therefore, in an era of enlightened rule,
by observing the music, one can know the customs; by observing the customs, one can know the governance;
and by observing the governance, one can know the ruler.
Therefore, the former kings invariably entrusted themselves to music in order to elucidate their teachings.
The zither used in the "Clear Temple" sacrifice
had red strings and wide spaces between them;
one would sing and sigh thrice,
which shows advancement in music.
In the ritual of the great feast,
the supreme offering was dark water in a vase and raw fish on a platter;
the thick soup was not seasoned,
which shows advancement in flavor.
Therefore, when the former kings established ritual and music,
it was not solely to please the eyes and ears or to gratify the desires of the mouth and stomach,
but to teach the people to regulate their likes and dislikes
and to practice reason and righteousness.
5.5 Ancient Music
It is said: Music comes from honoring;
it must not be abandoned.
It can be restrained or extravagant,
righteous or licentious.
The wise flourish through it,
while the unworthy perish.
In ancient times, when Zhu Xiangshi governed the world,
there were many winds and yang energy accumulated.
All things scattered and disintegrated,
and fruits did not ripen.
Therefore, Shi Da made a five-stringed zither
to bring forth yin energy
and stabilize all living things.
In ancient times, the music of the Ge Tian clan
involved three people holding an ox tail and stomping their feet, singing eight songs:
The first was "Carry the People,"
the second was "Profound Body,"
the third was "Accomplish the Grasses and Trees,"
the fourth was "Stir Up the Five Grains,"
the fifth was "Respect the Constant of Heaven,"
the sixth was "Achieve the Emperor's Merit,"
the seventh was "Rely on the Virtue of Earth,"
and the eighth was "Sum Up the Extremes of All Things."
In ancient times, at the beginning of the reign of Emperor Yao,
yin energy was abundant, stagnant, and accumulated,
the path of yang was blocked
and did not proceed in its proper order,
the people's qi was depressed, stifled, and stagnant,
and their sinews and bones contracted and did not stretch.
Therefore, dances were created to guide and release it.
Formerly, the Yellow Emperor ordered Ling Lun to create the musical scales.
Ling Lun went west from Daxia,
to the north of Ruanyou,
and obtained bamboo from the valley of Xiexi.
He selected bamboo that had consistent air passages, thickness, and evenness.
He cut between two nodes, making them three cun and nine fen in length, and blew into it.
This he made into the Yellow Bell pitch,
and the sound when blown was called "She Shao."
Next, he made twelve tubes,
and brought them to the foot of Ruanyou,
to listen to the songs of the phoenix,
in order to differentiate the twelve musical pitches.
The male phoenix sang six notes,
and the female phoenix also sang six notes.
These were compared to the Yellow Bell pitch, and they matched perfectly.
The Yellow Bell pitch
can be used to generate all the other pitches,
therefore it is called the Yellow Bell pitch,
the foundation of the musical scales.
The Yellow Emperor also ordered Ling Lun and Rong Jiang to cast twelve bells,
to harmonize the five tones,
in order to perform the "Ying Shao" music.
In the second month of spring,
on the day of Yi Mao,
when the sun was in Kui,
they began to play it.
It was named "Xian Chi".
Emperor Zhuanxu was born beside the Ruoshui River,
in fact residing in Kongsang,
and thus ascended to become Emperor.
In accordance with Heaven's harmony,
when the correct winds prevailed, they would move,
their sound like *xi xi qi qi qiang qiang*.
Emperor Zhuanxu loved this sound,
and thus ordered Feilong to create music imitating the sound of the eight winds,
calling it "Chengyun,"
to use in sacrifices to the Supreme God.
He then ordered Shanxian to be the first to lead the music;
Shanxian then lay down and reclined,
using its tail to drum its belly,
its sound *ying ying*.
Emperor Ku ordered Xian Hei to create sounds, singing
"Nine Summons," "Six Rows," and "Six Heroes."
There was Chui who made *pí*, drums, bells, chimes, *líng* pipes, *xūn*, *chí*, rattles, mallets, and hanging bells.
Emperor Ku then ordered people to clap or beat the *pí*,
strike the bells and chimes,
blow the *líng*, display the pipes, and play the *chí*.
Consequently, he ordered the phoenix and the celestial pheasant to dance to it.
Emperor Ku was greatly pleased,
and thus promoted Emperor Kang's virtue.
Emperor Yao ascended the throne,
and then ordered Zhi to create music.
Zhi then imitated the sounds of mountains, forests, streams, and valleys to create songs,
He then covered earthen jars with elk and deer hides and beat them.
Then he struck stones against stones
to imitate the sound of the jade chimes of the Supreme God,
in order to attract the dancing of all beasts.
Gu Sou then discarded the five-stringed zither
and made it into a fifteen-stringed zither.
He named it "Great Chapter"
to sacrifice to the Supreme God.
When Shun came to power,
he ordered Yan to discard the zither made by Gu Sou,
adding eight strings to it,
making it a twenty-three-stringed zither.
Emperor Shun then ordered Zhi to compose the "Nine Summons," "Six Arrays," and "Six Heroes"
to illuminate the virtue of the emperor.
When Yu came to power,
he diligently labored for the world,
tirelessly day and night.
He dredged the great rivers,
cleared blockages,
chiseled the Dragon Gate,
and lowered and opened up the Liao River to guide the Yellow River.
He dredged the Three Rivers and Five Lakes,
emptying them into the East Sea,
to benefit the black-haired people.
Thereupon, he ordered Gao Yao to create the "Xia Yue" dance in nine movements
to make his accomplishments manifest.
When Yin Tang ascended the throne,
the Xia dynasty was without principle,
tyrannical and cruel to the myriad people,
encroaching upon and diminishing the feudal lords,
not adhering to standards,
and the world suffered from it.
Thereupon, Tang led the six provinces to punish Jie's crimes,
his meritorious achievements were great,
and the black-haired people were at peace.
Tang then ordered Yi Yin to compose the "Great Protection,"
to sing the "Morning Dew,"
and to revise the "Nine Summons" and "Six Arrays,"
to display his goodness.
When King Wen of Zhou resided in Qi,
the feudal lords abandoned the three excesses of Yin and flocked to King Wen.
San Yisheng said:
"Yin can be attacked."
King Wen did not permit it.
Thereupon, the Duke of Zhou composed a poem, saying:
"King Wen is on high,
shining brightly in the heavens,
Zhou, though an old state,
its mandate is renewed,"
in order to guide the virtue of King Wen.
When King Wu ascended the throne,
He used the six armies to attack Yin,
but the six armies had not yet arrived,
and he defeated them with elite troops at Muye.
Upon his return,
he presented the captured prisoners and severed heads at the Great Chamber of the capital,
and then ordered the Duke of Zhou to compose the "Great Martial (Dance)."
When King Cheng came to the throne,
the people of Yin rebelled,
and the King ordered the Duke of Zhou to go and suppress them.
The Shang people trained elephants,
and committed atrocities among the Eastern Yi tribes,
so the Duke of Zhou then led an army to drive them away,
as far as the area south of the Yangtze River,
and then composed the "Three Elephants,"
to praise his virtue.
Therefore, the origins of music are ancient,
and not solely created by one generation.
Ji Xia Ji, Chapter Six
6.1 *Ji Xia Ji*
It says: In the month of Ji Xia (Late Summer):
The sun is in Willow,
the Xin star is at dusk,
the Kui star is at dawn.
Its days are Bing and Ding.
Its emperor is the Yan Emperor.
Its god is Zhurong.
Its insect is the feathered one.
Its musical note is Zhi.
The musical pitch corresponds to Lin Zhong.
Its number is seven.
Its taste is bitter.
Its smell is burnt.
Its sacrifice is to the stove.
The first offering is the lungs.
Cool breezes begin to arrive.
Crickets dwell in houses.
Eagles then begin to learn (to hunt).
Rotten grass transforms into fireflies.
The Son of Heaven dwells in the right chamber of the Bright Hall,
rides a vermilion carriage,
yokes red-black horses,
carries a red flag,
wears vermilion robes,
adorns red jade,
eats beans and chicken.
Its vessels are tall and rough.
In this month,
he orders the fishermen to hunt jiao dragons
and catch alligators, offer up turtles, and take soft-shelled turtles.
Then he orders the foresters to gather reeds and rushes.
In this month,
the four supervising ministers are ordered to collect the grain and fodder taxes from the hundred counties to feed the sacrificial animals.
The people are ordered to exert all their strength
to provide offerings to the great Heaven and supreme God,
the famous mountains and great rivers, and the gods of the four directions, to worship the spirits of the ancestral temples and altars of the soil and grain,
and to pray for blessings for the people.
In this month,
the female officials are ordered to dye fabrics,
creating elaborate and ornate designs.
They must follow the proper methods,
without any deviation or error.
Black, yellow, blue, and red
must all be of good quality.
No one should dare to use counterfeit or inferior materials
to provide clothing for suburban altars, temples, and sacrificial ceremonies,
and to make banners and emblems, to distinguish the degrees of nobility and rank.
In this month,
trees and plants are flourishing,
and the yin force is about to begin to inflict punishment. Therefore, the foresters are ordered to enter the mountains to inspect the trees, and no one should cut them down.
It is not permissible to undertake construction projects,
it is not permissible to convene the feudal lords,
it is not permissible to raise troops or mobilize the masses.
Do not undertake great affairs
in order to nurture the yang energy.
Do not issue decrees that interfere with the seasons,
so as not to hinder the affairs of Shen Nong (the god of agriculture).
When floods and heavy rains flourish,
he commands Shennong
to lead an inspection of achievements.
Undertaking great affairs will bring heavenly disasters.
In this month,
the soil is moist, and the heat is humid,
heavy rains occur frequently.
Burning and clearing is done to channel the water,
advantageous for killing weeds,
as if with hot water.
It can fertilize fields and paddies,
it can enrich the soil borders.
If this decree is carried out,
in this month, sweet rain will arrive three times,
every ten days and two days.
If in late summer, the commands of spring are implemented,
then the grains will loosen and fall,
the country will have much coughing,
and the people will migrate.
If the commands of autumn are implemented,
then the hills and damp places will have floods,
and the crops will not ripen,
and there will be many female disasters.
If the commands of winter are implemented,
then the cold air will be untimely,
the hawks and falcons will prey early,
The four borders enter for protection.
The Central Earth:
Its days are Earth-Yang (戊) and Earth-Yin (己).
Its Emperor is the Yellow Emperor.
Its spirit is Houtu (后土, the Queen of Earth).
Its creature is the naked (i.e., humans).
Its note is Gong (宮).
The musical pitch corresponds to the Gong of the Yellow Bell.
Its number is five.
Its taste is sweet.
Its smell is fragrant.
Its sacrifice is at the Central Niche (中霤).
The sacrifice is offered first to the Heart.
The Son of Heaven resides in the Grand Hall of the Great Temple,
rides the Great Carriage,
is drawn by yellow-red horses,
carries the yellow banner,
wears yellow clothes,
adorns himself with yellow jade,
and eats millet and beef.
Its vessels are round and cover (i.e., have lids).
6.2 Music and Pitch
The second section says:
The Yellow Bell generates the Forest Bell (林鐘),
the Forest Bell generates the Great Cluster (太蔟),
the Great Cluster generates the Southern Lü (南呂),
Nanlü generates Guxi,
Guxi generates Yingzhong,
Yingzhong generates Ruibin,
Ruibin generates Dalü,
Dalü generates Yize,
Yize generates Jiazhong,
Jiazhong generates Wushe,
Wushe generates Zhonglü.
What is generated by dividing by three
is increased by one-third to generate upwards;
what is generated by dividing by three
has one-third removed to generate downwards.
Huangzhong, Dalü, Taicou, Jiazhong, Guxi, Zhonglü, and Ruibin are above; Linzhong, Yize, Nanlü, Wushe, and Yingzhong are below.
In the age of great sages and ultimate principles,
the qi of Heaven and Earth
combine to generate wind.
When the sun reaches its limit, the moon gathers its wind,
to generate the twelve lü.
In midwinter, the days are shortest,
then Huangzhong is generated.
In late winter, Dalü is generated.
In early spring, Taicou is generated.
In mid-spring, Jiazhong is generated.
In late spring, Guxi is generated.
In early summer, Zhonglü is generated.
In midsummer, the days are longest,
then Ruibin is generated.
In the last month of summer, Lin Zhong arises.
In the first month of autumn, Yi Ze arises.
In the second month of autumn, Nan Lü arises.
In the last month of autumn, Wu Yi arises.
In the first month of winter, Ying Zhong arises.
When the wind and qi of Heaven and Earth are correct,
then the twelve lü (musical pipes) are determined.
In the month of Huang Zhong,
there should be no earthworks undertaken.
Be careful not to open covers,
in order to secure the closing of Heaven and Earth.
To open covers and expose stores,
to mobilize large crowds,
the yang qi will be released,
this is called opening the chambers of Heaven and Earth.
In the month of Da Lü,
the counting of years will almost end,
the year will soon begin again,
and focus is solely on agriculture, the people
should not be employed elsewhere.
In the month of Tai Cu,
the qi of Heaven descends, the yang qi begins to arise,
Heaven and Earth are in harmony, grasses and trees flourish,
order the farmers to cultivate the soil,
do not let them miss the season.
In the month of Jia Zhong,
be generous, broad-minded, and peaceful,
Practice virtue and abandon punishments;
let no one undertake actions
that harm the multitude of living beings.
In the month of Guxi (first month),
open roads and clear pathways;
repair and dredge ditches and canals.
Promulgate this order repeatedly,
and auspicious influences will hasten to arrive.
In the month of Zhonglü (second month),
do not gather large crowds,
but inspect and encourage agricultural work.
As grasses and trees are just beginning to grow,
do not unsettle the hearts of the people.
In the month of Ruibin (fifth month),
the yang energy is above,
so ensure the robust are cared for and the clever nurtured.
If the court is not at peace,
the grasses and trees will wither prematurely.
In the month of Linzhong (sixth month),
the grasses and trees are lush and flourishing,
and yin energy will begin to bring punishments.
Do not initiate grand enterprises,
in order to usher in the yang energy.
In the month of Yize (seventh month),
refine the laws and administer punishments;
select warriors and hone the troops;
investigate and punish the unrighteous,
in order to pacify distant regions.
In the month of Nanlü,
hibernating insects all bow down in their burrows,
and all seal up their doors. Urge the farmers to harvest and gather,
daring not to be lazy,
making abundance their aim.
In the month of Wushe,
swiftly judge the guilty,
when the law is applicable, grant no pardon,
do not prolong lawsuits,
making speed the priority.
In the month of Yingzhong,
Yin and Yang do not communicate,
closing off to become winter.
Regulate and distinguish mourning rituals,
distinguish clothing, and examine where the people will end their lives.
6.3 *Yin Chu*
Thirdly:
The Xia dynasty ruler Kongjia was hunting in the Dongyang Mountain,
when a great wind and darkness obscured everything,
Kongjia was lost and confused,
and entered a commoner's house.
The master of the house was then giving birth.
Some said,
"The future will be a good day,
this child will surely be very lucky."
Others said,
"It will not be able to overcome [bad fortune],
"This child is sure to bring disaster."
Afterwards, she took the child and returned,
saying,
"Thinking he is my child,
who would dare bring disaster upon him?"
The child grew up,
moved a curtain, pulled down a rafter,
and an axe chopped off his foot,
and he became a gatekeeper.
Kong Jia said,
"Alas!
It is fate,
it is ordained!"
Then he composed the song "Broken Axe,"
and this was the origin of Eastern music.
Yu was performing his labors,
and saw a daughter of the Tu Shan.
Yu did not meet her but went on to inspect the southern lands.
The daughter of the Tu Shan clan then ordered her concubine to go and wait for Yu on the south side of Tu Shan.
The woman then made a song,
singing, "Waiting for a man, oh!"
This was the origin of Southern music.
The Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao collected airs,
and made them into the "Zhou Nan" and "Shao Nan."
King Zhao of Zhou personally led an expedition to conquer Jing.
Xin Yumi was tall and strong,
He served as a king's right-hand man.
Later, he turned back and crossed the Han River.
When Liang was defeated,
the king and Cai Gong were rescued in Hanzhong.
Xin Yu Mi, King Zhen's follower, crossed the river to the north,
and also helped Zhen and Cai Gong.
Duke Zhou then enfeoffed him in the Western Di,
making him the eldest Duke.
Yin Zheng Jia moved his residence to the west of the Yellow River,
but still longed for his old home.
He was the first to create the Western sounds.
The eldest Duke continued this sound, living in the Western Mountains.
Duke Mu of Qin adopted the style of this music,
and was the first to create the Qin music.
The You Song clan had two unmarried women,
for whom they built a nine-tiered platform.
They ate and drank always with drums.
The Emperor ordered a swallow to go and observe them.
It chirped like a stifled sound.
The two women loved it and fought to catch it,
covering it with a jade basket.
After a short while,
they opened it to look,
and the swallow had left behind two eggs.
It flew north,
and never returned.
The two women composed a song, the first ending
It is said,
"Swallows fly away,"
which was in fact the beginning of northern music.
All music,
originates from the human heart.
When moved within the heart, it manifests as sound;
sound forms externally and transforms internally.
Therefore, by hearing the sound, one knows the customs;
by observing the customs, one knows the aspirations;
by observing the aspirations, one knows the virtue.
Prosperity and decline, the worthy and unworthy, the gentleman and the petty person, all are shaped in music;
they cannot be hidden.
Therefore, it is said that music is a profound observation.
If the soil is exhausted, grass and trees will not grow;
if the water is turbulent, fish and turtles will not grow large;
if the world is turbid, rites become complicated and music becomes licentious.
The sounds of Zheng and Wei,
the music of Sangjian,
these are what disordered states love,
what decaying virtue delights in.
When sounds of deviation, perversion, extravagance, and excess emerge,
then a sense of overflowing indulgence and a heart of depraved arrogance will be felt. When felt, then all kinds of wickedness and manifold deviations will arise from this.
Therefore, the gentleman reverts to the Way to cultivate virtue,
rectifies virtue to produce music,
and harmonizes music to achieve obedience.
When the music is harmonious, the people will turn towards the right direction.
6.4 《Zhi Le》
Four said:
If you want to observe supreme music,
you must look to supreme order.
If the order is substantial, the music will be substantial;
if the order is insubstantial, the music will be insubstantial;
in a chaotic world, music will be lax.
Now, if one closes the doors and windows of a room,
and it can move heaven and earth,
it is merely a single room.
Therefore, in the time of Cheng Tang,
grain grew in the courtyard,
sprouting at dusk
and becoming a large armful by dawn.
His historian requested to divine the reason for this.
Tang dismissed the diviner, saying,
"I have heard that auspicious signs are the forerunners of blessings;
if one sees an auspicious sign and does not act virtuously, blessings will not arrive.
Portents are the forerunners of misfortune;
if one sees a portent and acts virtuously, misfortune will not arrive."
Thereupon, he held early morning audiences and late evening retirements,
inquired about the sick and offered condolences to the bereaved,
striving to pacify the common people.
After three days, the grain vanished on its own.
Thus, misfortune is what fortune relies upon,
and fortune is where misfortune lies hidden.
The sage alone sees this,
how would the masses know its limit?
In the eighth year of King Wen of Zhou's establishment of his state,
in the sixth month of the year,
King Wen was bedridden with illness for five days, and the earth shook.
East, west, south, north,
it did not extend beyond the borders of the state.
All the officials requested, saying:
"Your servants have heard that the shaking of the earth
is for the sake of the ruler.
Now the king has been bedridden with illness for five days, and the earth shakes, on all sides not going beyond the suburbs of Zhou.
All the ministers are afraid, and say, 'We beg you to move it away.'"
King Wen said:
"How can we move it away?"
They replied:
"Raise undertakings and mobilize the masses
to increase the walls of the state,
can this move it away?"
King Wen said:
"No.
When Heaven shows a portent,
it is to punish the guilty.
I must have committed a crime,
therefore Heaven punishes me with this.
Now, if we intentionally raise undertakings and mobilize the masses to increase the walls of the state,
this is to increase my guilt.
It is not allowed." King Wen said,
"It is through this that I will flourish.
Please, let us change our behavior and emphasize goodness to move it away.
Could it be avoided?"
Thereupon, he was careful with his rituals, ranks, and leather goods,
in order to interact with the various lords;
he refined his words and speeches,
his gifts of silk and jade,
in order to treat worthy gentlemen with respect;
he distributed his ranks, positions, levels, fields, and lands,
in order to reward those who had contributed, and subsequently did so with his ministers.
Having implemented this for not very long,
the sickness then stopped.
King Wen had been enthroned for eight years when an earthquake occurred.
Forty-three years after the earthquake,
in total, King Wen established the state for fifty-one years before he died.
This is how King Wen stopped disasters and eliminated portents.
During the time of Duke Jing of Song,
Mars was in the Heart constellation.
The Duke was afraid
and summoned Zi Wei to ask him about it,
saying:
"Mars is in the Heart constellation.
What does this mean?"
Zi Wei said:
"Mars is
a heavenly punishment;
the Heart constellation is
the assigned territory of Song.
Disaster will likely fall upon your person.
Although,
it can be transferred to the Prime Minister."
The Duke said:
"The Prime Minister is the one who governs the state with me,
and to transfer death to him
is inauspicious."
Zi Wei said:
"It can be transferred to the people."
The Duke said:
"If the people die,
who will I be ruler over?
I would rather die alone."
Zi Wei said:
"It can be transferred to the year."
The Duke said:
"If the year is harmful, the people will be hungry,
and if the people are hungry, they will surely die.
If I, as a ruler, desire to kill my people in order to save myself,
who would take me as their ruler?
It seems that my fate is truly exhausted,
do not speak of it again."
Zi Wei turned and walked away,
faced north, bowed, and said:
"Your servant dares to congratulate you, my lord.
Heaven is high and listens to the low.
You have three words of supreme virtue,
Heaven will surely grant you three rewards.
Tonight, Mars will move three houses,
Lord Yan Nian is twenty-one years old."
The Duke said:
"How do you know this?"
He replied:
"For three good pieces of advice,
there must be three rewards.
The planet Mars has shifted its lodge three times,
each lodge passing by seven stars.
Each shift of a star corresponds to one year.
Three times seven is twenty-one.
Therefore, I said Lord Yan Nian is twenty-one years old.
I request to lie in wait for it before Your Majesty.
If Mars does not shift,
I request to die for it."
The Duke said:
"Permitted."
That very night, Mars indeed shifted three lodges.
6.5 "Understanding Principles"
Fifthly:
The Five Emperors and Three Kings have exhausted the principles of music.
The rulers of disordered states
have never understood music;
they are ordinary rulers.
To have a heavenly reward and attain rulership,

This is like sitting upright in a dark room;

For all that lives is not the transformation of a single Qi,

What they consider pleasure,

Husbands and wives deceive each other,
