there is Mars (熒惑),
there is a comet,
there is the Celestial Pestle (天棓),
there is the Celestial Broom (天欃),
there is the Celestial Bamboo (天竹),
there is the Celestial Hero (天英),
there is the Celestial Stem (天干),
there is the Robber Star (賊星),
there is the Fighting Star (鬭星),
there is a Guest Star (賓星).
Concerning the qi,
there is that which above does not belong to the sky,
and below does not belong to the earth,
there is abundance above and killing below,
there is that which is like the waves of water,
there is that which is like the mast of a mountain.
In spring it is yellow,
in summer it is black,
in autumn it is grey-green,
in winter it is red.
Its strange and monstrous occurrences:
some are born resembling belts,
some ghosts throw themselves against its walls,
some hares give birth to pheasants,
pheasants also give birth to sparrows,
some rice borers gather in its state,
their sound is *xiong xiong*,
in the state there are wandering snakes going west and east,
horses and cattle speak,
dogs and pigs connect together,
some wolves enter into the state,
some men descend from the sky,
in the market there are dancing owls,
in the state there are flying movements,
horses are born with horns,
roosters have five legs,
some pigs are born with umbilical cords intact,
many chicken eggs are addled,
some earth shrines move their location,
some pigs give birth to dogs.
If a state has these things occur,
and its ruler does not know to be alarmed and quickly reform,
the Supreme God will send down calamity,
and misfortune will certainly be swift.
Their remaining people died and were lost,
utterly extinguished without a trace,
scattered and wandering, facing starvation every day.
All of this is produced by a state in disorder;
it is impossible to count,
even if all the bamboo of Jing and Yue
were used, it would still be impossible to write it all down.
Therefore, Zihua Zi said:
"The people of a chaotic world
are short and awkward, suffer from all kinds of diseases,
many people suffer from epidemics,
the roads are full of swaddling clothes,
the blind, bald, hunchbacked, and lame,
all kinds of strange things are born."
Therefore, how could a ruler of a chaotic world
hear of supreme joy?
If he does not hear of supreme joy,
his joy is not joy.
Book of Mid-Autumn, Seventh
7.1 "Book of Mid-Autumn"
It is said:
In the month of Mid-Autumn:
the summer solstice is forty-six days past.
The sun is in Wing,
at dusk, the Dipper is in the middle,
at dawn, the Hyades are in the middle.
Then comes the Beginning of Autumn. Its days are Geng and Xin.
Its emperor is Shaohao.
Its god is Rushou.
Its creature is the furry animal.
Its musical note is Shang.
The musical pipe corresponds to Yi Ze.
Its number is nine.
Its flavor is pungent.
Its smell is rancid.
Its sacrifice is to the door.
The first offering is the liver.
Cool winds arrive.
White dew descends.
Cold cicadas chirp.
Eagles then sacrifice birds.
It is the beginning of employing and executing punishments.
The Son of Heaven resides in the left pavilion of the Zongzhang Hall,
rides the war chariot, yokes white camels,
carries a white banner,
wears white clothing,
adorns himself with white jade,
eats hemp seeds and dog.
Its vessels are simple and deep.
In this month,
the Beginning of Autumn occurs.
Three days before the Beginning of Autumn,
the Grand Historian informs the Son of Heaven,
saying:
"On a certain day, the Autumn Solstice arrives,
the flourishing virtue resides in Metal."
The Son of Heaven then fasts.
On the day of the Autumn Solstice,
the Son of Heaven personally leads the Three Dukes, Nine Ministers, feudal lords, and grand officers to greet the autumn in the western suburbs.
Upon returning,
he then rewards the military leaders and warriors at court.
The Son of Heaven then commands the generals and commanders
to select soldiers, sharpen weapons,
and examine the outstanding talents;
to exclusively appoint those with merit,
in order to punish injustice;
to investigate and execute the tyrannical and disrespectful,
in order to make clear likes and dislikes;
and to patrol those distant lands.
In this month,
he orders the officials
to revise laws and regulations,
to repair prisons,
to prepare fetters and handcuffs,
to prohibit villainy,
to be careful of crimes and evil,
and to focus on capturing offenders.
He orders those who administer justice
to examine injuries and investigate wounds,
to inspect fractures and judge with precision;
to settle lawsuits
Must be upright and impartial;
Execute the guilty,
Strictly determine punishments.
Heaven and earth begin to become stern,
One must not be excessive.
In this month,
Farmers then bring up the grain.
The Son of Heaven tastes the new grain,
First presenting it to the ancestral temple.
He commands the officials
to begin the harvest and storage.
Complete the embankments,
Carefully secure the blockages,
To prepare for floods and heavy rains.
Repair palaces and houses,
Repair the walls and fences,
Mend the city walls.
In this month,
Do not enfeoff lords or establish high officials, do not cede land,
Bestow heavy gifts, or send out great envoys.
If one carries out these orders,
Then the cool wind will arrive in thirty days.
If in early autumn one carries out winter commands,
Then the yin energy will greatly overcome,
Armored insects will ruin the grain,
Then the soldiers of the Rong people came.
If we enact the ordinances of spring,
then their country will suffer drought.
The yang energy will return,
and the five grains will not ripen.
If we enact the ordinances of summer,
then there will be many fires.
Cold and heat will be out of balance,
and the people will suffer much from malaria.
7.2 "Controlling Soldiers"
Secondly,
the ancient sage kings had righteous armies but never had armies that were put to rest (completely abolished).
The origin of armies is ancient;
it exists together with the beginning of the people.
Generally speaking, the army
is power (威);
and power
is strength (力).
The people's possession of power and strength is in their nature.
This nature is what is received from Heaven,
and is not something that humans can create.
The martial cannot change it,
and the artisan cannot move it.
The origin of armies is ancient.
Huangdi and Yandi already used water and fire.
Gonggong shi already repeatedly created difficulties.
The Five Emperors already fought with each other.
Dynasties rise and fall,
the victor takes control.
It is also said, "Chiyou created weapons,"
but Chiyou did not create weapons;
he merely improved upon them.
Before the time of Chiyou,
the people already stripped forests for wood to fight with, and the victor became the leader.
The leader was still insufficient to govern them,
so they established a lord.
The lord was still insufficient to govern them,
so they established a Son of Heaven.
The establishment of the Son of Heaven came from the lord,
the establishment of the lord came from the leader,
and the establishment of the leader came from conflict.
The source of conflict and fighting has been around for a long time,
it cannot be prohibited,
it cannot be stopped.
Therefore, the sage kings of old had righteous armies but never ceased warfare.
If a household has no angry scolding,
then the faults of young children will immediately be seen;
if a state has no punishments,
then the people's acts of mutual aggression will immediately be seen;
if the world has no punitive expeditions,
then the princes' acts of mutual violence will immediately be seen.
Therefore, angry scolding cannot be abolished in the household,
punishments cannot be abolished in the state,
punitive expeditions cannot be abolished in the world;
It is simply a matter of skill and clumsiness.
Therefore, the sage kings of old had righteous armies but never abolished armies.
To want to prohibit all food in the world because someone died from overeating
is absurd;
to want to prohibit all boats in the world because someone died while riding a boat
is absurd;
to want to abolish all weapons in the world because someone lost their state through the use of weapons
is absurd.
That weapons cannot be abolished
is like water and fire:
if used well, they bring good fortune;
if used poorly, they bring disaster.
It is the same with those who use medicine well:
if they obtain good medicine, they save people;
if they obtain bad medicine, they kill people.
Righteous armies are like good medicine for the world, and their importance is great indeed.
Moreover, the origin of weapons goes back far;
there has never been a moment when they were not used.
Noble and base, old and young, wise and foolish all share in them;
there is only a difference between the great and the small.
Observe the minute aspects of warfare:
Intent held in the heart but not yet expressed is
warfare;
a fierce look is warfare;
a change of countenance is warfare;
arrogant speech is warfare;
drawing someone near or pushing someone away is warfare;
repeated betrayal is warfare;
extravagant competition is warfare;
the three armies attacking and battling is warfare.
These eight are all warfare,
whether the contention be small or large.
Those in the present age who speak hastily of putting down arms,
use warfare their entire lives without realizing it, which is absurd.
Therefore, though their arguments are strong,
though their discussions are eloquent,
though their literary knowledge is vast,
they still are not listened to.
Therefore, the ancient sage kings had righteous warfare
but none who put down arms.
If warfare is truly righteous,
used to punish tyrannical rulers and uplift suffering people,
the people's joy at it
is like a filial son seeing a loving parent,
like a hungry person seeing delicious food;
the people's shouting and rushing toward it
is like a powerful crossbow shot into a deep ravine,
like accumulating great water and losing its containing dike.
Even a mediocre ruler would still be able to possess his people,
How much more so is this true of a tyrannical ruler?
7.3 *Quelling Disorder*
Third,
the present age
is extremely corrupt,
and the suffering of the common people
cannot be increased any further.
The Son of Heaven is already cut off (from power),
virtuous men are discarded and hidden,
the rulers of the world act as they please,
separating themselves from the people,
and the common people have nowhere to turn to for redress.
If there are wise rulers and outstanding scholars in the world,
they should carefully examine this argument,
then their armies will be armies of righteousness.
The people of the world
will be like those who are about to die and yet live,
like those who are about to be disgraced and yet be honored,
like those who are about to suffer and yet be at ease.
If the rulers of the world act as they please,
then even men of average character will flee their rulers and abandon their relatives,
how much more so will those who are worthless?
Therefore, when an army of righteousness arrives,
the ruler of the world will be unable to hold onto his people,
and relatives will be unable to restrain their sons.
In general, being a leader of the people of the world,
there is no greater consideration than promoting those who possess the Way and suppressing those who are without the Way,
Reward what is righteous, and punish what is unrighteous.
In the present age,
scholars mostly disapprove of military attacks.
If one disapproves of military attacks, yet advocates for defense,

then if one advocates for defense, the methods that local leaders call "promoting the moral and curbing the immoral," and "rewarding the righteous and punishing the unrighteous" cannot be put into practice.
The benefits and harms to those who govern the people of the world
depend on carefully examining this argument.
Military attacks and defense are essentially the same thing,
yet people differ in what they choose to accept or reject.
They use persuasive arguments to dismiss it,
and ultimately arrive at no definitive conclusion.
This is surely due to not understanding,
which is foolish;
or understanding but deceiving one's heart,
which is fraudulent.
For those who are fraudulent and foolish,
even if they argue, it is useless.
They deem wrong what should be accepted, and accept what should be deemed wrong.
This is benefiting what should be harmed,
and securing what should be endangered.
Such arguments, if they are considered profound,
become the greatest cause of trouble for the world, and bring the greatest harm to the common people.
Therefore, those who have the benefit of the people of the world at heart
cannot but thoroughly examine this argument.
Now, in the matter of military attacks,
there has never been a case where the immoral were not attacked and the unrighteous were not punished.
To attack the immoral and punish the unrighteous
Then there would be no greater fortune,
and the common people would reap no greater benefit.
To prohibit it
is to suppress the way of virtue and attack the cause of righteousness; it is to bring to ruin the achievements of Tang and Wu and perpetuate the errors of Jie and Zhou.
The reason why people detest being without virtue and unrighteous
is because of the punishment it brings;
the reason why they aspire to be virtuous and act righteously
is because of the reward it brings.
Now, if being without virtue and unrighteousness persists,
and those who are so are rewarded,
while being virtuous and acting righteously are driven to ruin,
and those who are so are punished,
rewarding evil and punishing good,
and yet desiring the people to be well-governed,
is that not difficult?
Therefore, those who throw the world into chaos and harm the common people
are best discussed as being great.
7.4 "Blocking Up"
Fourthly:
As for the mindset of defending and guarding,
there has never been a case of not defending the way of no virtue and guarding the way of unrighteousness.
To defend the way of no virtue and guard the way of unrighteousness
is the greatest misfortune,
and the deepest harm to the people of the world.
In general, in defense and guarding,
the highest approach is through persuasion,
Next comes the use of arms.
If persuasion results in widespread acceptance and adherence,
one should contemplate it day and night,
meticulously devoting oneself to the task.
When awake, one should recite it;
when asleep, one should dream of it.
One should exert oneself to the point of parching the lips and drying the lungs,
exhausting the mind and wounding the spirit.
One should cite the achievements of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors to please the ruler,
and mention the strategies of the Five Hegemons and famous figures to lend credence to the matter.
One should attend court early and leave late,
reporting to the one who plans the military action
and spreading the message to the masses to clarify the principles.
If, after all efforts, the persuasion remains isolated and ineffective,
then one must inevitably resort to arms.
Resorting to arms
inevitably leads to conflict and strife.
The nature of conflict and strife
invariably involves killing.
This amounts to killing innocent people to support those who are without principle and unjust.
For the unprincipled and unjust to prevail
is to foster harm and suppress benefit to the world.
Even if one were to fortunately achieve victory,
calamity would only begin to grow.
The law of the former kings states:
"Reward those who do good,
punish those who do evil."
This is the ancient way,
Cannot be changed.
Now, to not distinguish between what is right and what is wrong,
and hastily resort to seizing, attacking, defending,
there is no greater unrighteousness,
and there is nothing that harms the people of the world more severely.
Therefore, seizing and attacking cannot
be condemned,
attacking and seizing cannot
be undertaken,
defending and guarding cannot
be condemned,
defending and guarding cannot
be undertaken;
only righteous warfare is permissible.
If warfare is righteous,
attacking and seizing are also permissible,
and defending and guarding are also permissible.
If warfare is unrighteous,
attacking and seizing are not permissible,
and defending and guarding are not permissible.
That Xia Jie and Yin Zhou were unprincipled to such an extent
was due to luck;
that Wu Fucha and Zhi Boyao invaded and plundered to such an extent
was due to luck;
that Jin Li, Chen Ling, and Song Kang were wicked to such an extent
was due to luck.
If Jie and Zhou knew that they would certainly lose their kingdoms, die,
and have their lineage exterminated without any descendants,
I did not know that tyranny and lack of principle could reach such a degree.
King Fuchai of Wu and Zhi Bo Yao knew that their states would surely be reduced to ruins,
and their persons subjected to punishment and execution.
I did not know that their wickedness, lack of principle, encroachment, and plunder could reach such a degree.
Duke Li of Jin knew that he would surely die at the hands of the artisan Li Shi,
Duke Ling of Chen knew that he would surely die at the hands of Xia Zhengshu,
and Duke Kang of Song knew that he would surely die in Wen. I did not know that their wickedness could reach such a degree.
These seven rulers,
were exceedingly unprincipled and unjust:
the number of innocent people they slaughtered
cannot be counted in the tens of thousands.
The deaths of the strong, the young, the old, and even unborn fetuses,
filled the broad plains.
They piled (corpses) high in deep valleys and great ravines,
flung them into great rivers,
accumulated ashes (of cremated bodies),
filled ditches and dangerous places,
faced flying arrows,
trod on naked blades,
and added to this the suffering of freezing, starvation, hunger, and cold.
Even in this present age,
it is becoming even worse.
Therefore, the exposed bones are countless,
forming mounds like hills and mountains.
If there is an enlightened ruler or benevolent man in the world,
who deeply contemplates this,
it is enough to cause him pain,
it is enough to cause him grief.
Observe where this originates.
It originates from the abandonment of those who possess the Way
and the unrestrained actions of those who lack the Way.
The unrestrained actions of those who lack the Way
are fortunate indeed!
Therefore, the trouble in the world
lies not in rescue and defense,
but in the good fortune of the unworthy.
When the argument for rescue and defense emerges,
the unworthy become even more fortunate,
and the worthy become even more doubtful.
Therefore, what greatly disorders the world lies in hastily adopting rescue and defense without considering their righteousness.
7.5 "Cherishing Favor"
Fifthly:
Generally speaking, the explanations of gentlemen
are not merely for the sake of argument;
the deliberations of scholars
are not merely for the sake of talk.
They must hit the mark of reason before explaining,
and must be appropriate to righteousness before deliberating.
Therefore, if righteousness is explained, rulers and great men will increasingly love reason, and the common people will increasingly practice righteousness.
When the Way of righteousness and reason is made clear,
the methods of tyranny, deceit, and usurpation will cease.
Tyranny and deceit are opposed to righteousness and reason;
their power cannot both prevail,
they cannot coexist.
Therefore, when the army enters the enemy's territory,
the people know where to seek protection,
and the common people know they will not die.
Reaching the outskirts of towns and cities,
do not harm the five grains,
do not dig up graves,
do not cut down trees,
do not burn stockpiles,
do not burn houses,
do not seize domestic animals.
If you capture people, treat them well and send them back,
in order to show good and evil;
keep faith with the people,

in order to seize the enemy's resources. If, after all this, there are still those who harbor resentment, brave danger, continue in their errors, and refuse to listen, then even resorting to force is permissible.
First, make a proclamation and issue a declaration, saying:
"The army comes
to save the people from death.
Your ruler on high is without virtue,
arrogant, haughty, neglectful, and lazy,
greedy, violent, and cruel to the masses,
self-willed and arbitrary,
rejecting the ways of the sages,
despising and reviling the former kings,
rejecting and slandering the old laws,
not obeying Heaven above,
not benefiting the people below,
levying taxes without end,
To demand without satiety,
to unjustly kill the innocent,
to reward and punish improperly.
Those who act like this
are those whom Heaven will punish,
those whom the people will hate,
and are not fit to be rulers.
Now, the coming of our army
is to punish those who are not fit to be rulers,
to eliminate the people's hatred, and to follow the Way of Heaven.
If there are people who oppose the Way of Heaven and protect the enemies of the people,
they will be killed and their families exterminated without pardon.
Those who can listen with their families
will be rewarded with the possessions of a family;
those who listen with their neighborhoods
will be rewarded with the possessions of a neighborhood;
those who listen with their villages
will be rewarded with the possessions of a village;
those who listen with their towns
will be rewarded with the possessions of a town;
those who listen with their state
will be rewarded with the possessions of a state."
Therefore, when we conquer a state, we will not harm its people,
but will only punish those who deserve to be punished.
We will promote its outstanding scholars and enfeoff them as marquises,
select its virtuous and worthy men and honor and elevate them,
seek out its orphans and widows and provide relief for them,
and show respect and courtesy to its elders.
All were increased in their stipends,
and raised in their rank.
They judged their criminals and rescued them;
they divided the gold of the treasuries,
and distributed the grain of the granaries,
in order to pacify and soothe the masses,
not keeping the wealth for themselves;
they inquired about the populous local shrines and large ancestral temples,
and restored those that the people did not want abolished,
adding extensively to their sacrificial rites.
Therefore, the virtuous glorified their names,
the elders rejoiced in their rites,
and the people cherished their virtue.
Now, if there were a person here
who could bring a single person back from the dead,
then the world would certainly vie to serve him.
The righteous army revives more than just one person,
so who would not rejoice?
Therefore, when the righteous army arrives,
the people of neighboring states flock to it like flowing water,
and the people of the conquered state look to it as if it were their parents.
The farther they travel,
the more people they gain;
without a blade being crossed, the people submit as if transformed.
The Records of Mid-Autumn, Eighth Month
8.1 *The Records of Mid-Autumn*
First, it is said:
In the month of mid-autumn:
the sun is in the constellation Horn (角),
at dusk the Herdboy (牽牛) is in the middle (of the sky),
at dawn the Turtle Beak (觜嶲) is in the middle (of the sky).
Its days are Geng (庚) and Xin (辛).
Its emperor is Shao Hao (少皞).
Its god is Ru Shou (蓐收).
Its insect is the hairy one.
Its note is Shang (商).
The musical pitch corresponds to Nan Lü (南呂).
Its number is nine.
Its taste is pungent.
Its smell is rank.
It is sacrificed to the door.
Offer the liver first in sacrifice.
Cool winds arise.
Migratory geese arrive.
Dark swallows return (south).
The birds store up provisions.
The Son of Heaven resides in the Zongzhang Grand Temple (總章太廟),
rides in the war chariot,
is drawn by white camels,
carries the white banner,
wears white clothes,
wears white jade,
eats hemp seeds and dog meat.
Its vessels are unadorned and deep.
This month,
nourish the aged and feeble,
bestow stools and canes,
and provide millet gruel and other food and drink.
Then order the Minister of Clothing
to thoroughly prepare the garments,
with regular patterns of embroidery,
regulations for size,
standards for length,
and measured quantities of clothing,
necessarily following the old rules,
with regular caps and belts.
Order the officials
to strictly enforce all punishments,
and executions must be appropriate.
Do not bend or distort [justice].
If justice is bent or distorted inappropriately,
one will receive calamity in return.
This month,
order the stewards and priests
to inspect the sacrificial animals:
to see that they are complete;
to examine their fodder;
to observe their fatness;
to inspect their color;
they must be classified;
Measure the large and small,
Observe the long and short,
All meet the standard.
When these five are fully appropriate,
God will surely enjoy the offerings.
The Son of Heaven then performs the Nuo exorcism,
To ward off auxiliary diseases,
So as to facilitate the passage of autumn Qi.
Use dogs to taste hemp seeds,
First, sacrifice at the ancestral temple.
In this month,
One can build city walls,
Establish capitals,
Dig caves and cellars,
Repair granaries and storehouses.
Then order the officials
To urge the people to gather in the harvest,
Strive to store vegetables,
And accumulate many provisions.
Then encourage the planting of wheat,
Without missing the season;
If anyone misses the season, punish them without hesitation.
In this month,
Day and night are equal.
The thunder then begins to cease its sound.
Hibernating insects all bow down in their holes, all sealing their doors.
The killing aura is increasingly strong,
the yang energy wanes daily.
The water begins to dry up.
(When) day and night are of equal length,
then standardize measures,
level scales,
correct balances,
and align volumes.
In this month,
ease tariffs at the borders and markets,
attract merchants and travelers,
bring in goods and valuables,
in order to facilitate the people's affairs.
People from all directions come together,
distant regions all arrive,
then wealth and goods will not be lacking,
the government will have no shortage of resources,
and all affairs will be accomplished.
In all undertakings, do not go against the heavenly order,
you must follow the season,
and act according to their kind.
If you execute this command,
the white dew will fall in thirty days.
If in mid-autumn you execute the spring command,
then the autumn rain will not fall,
grasses and trees will flourish,
The state would then have great fear.
If the summer season's orders are carried out,
then the state will have drought,
hibernating insects will not hide away,
and the five grains will sprout again (out of season).
If the winter season's orders are carried out,
then wind disasters will arise frequently,
thunder will occur before it is due,
and plants and trees will die early.
8.2 *On Authority*
Secondly, it is said:
Righteousness is
the guideline for all matters,
the source from which the relationship between ruler and minister, superiors and inferiors, intimacy and distance arises,
and the place where order, chaos, safety, danger, excess, and victory reside.
Overcome excess;
do not seek it from others;
it must be reflected upon oneself.
Human nature desires life and hates death,
desires glory and hates disgrace.
If the principle of life and death, glory and disgrace, is unified,
then the soldiers of the three armies can be made to be of one mind.
In general, an army desires a large number of soldiers,
and the mind desires unity.
If the three armies are of one mind, then orders can be made invincible.
If one can ensure invincibility,
then one's army will also be invincible throughout the world.
The ultimate form of warfare in ancient times
placed great importance on commands from the people.
They valued the world,
and revered the emperor.
These commands were stored in the hearts of the people,
and were as swift as the movement of their own skin.
The people held them with deep pain and unwavering resolve,
and could not be swayed or shaken.
Nothing could move them.
If this were the case, what enemy would be worth defeating?
Therefore, it is said that if one's commands are strong, then one's enemy is weak;
and if one's commands are trustworthy, then one's enemy will yield.
If victory is first achieved here,
then victory will surely be achieved there.
Generally speaking, weapons
are the most ominous tools in the world;
and courage
is the most ominous virtue in the world.
To wield ominous tools
and practice ominous virtues
is only permissible as a last resort.
Wielding ominous tools must lead to killing;
killing
is done to preserve life.
Practicing ominous virtues must lead to awe;
Majesty
is what is used to intimidate.
When the enemy is intimidated, the people prosper;
this is why righteous armies flourish.
Therefore, the ultimate armies of ancient times,
before the talent of the people was combined,
majesty had already been communicated,
and the enemy had already submitted.
Why necessarily use drumsticks, shields, and spears?
Therefore, one who is good at communicating majesty
does so before it is manifested,
before it is made known.
Dark and obscure,
none know the true situation;
this is called the sincerity of ultimate majesty.
In general, warfare requires urgency, speed, and preemptiveness.
The way to achieve urgency, speed, and preemptiveness
lies in understanding the distinction between slowness, deliberation, and tardiness on the one hand, and urgency, speed, and preemptiveness on the other.
Urgency, speed, and preemptiveness
are the means by which righteous armies secure victory.
And it is imperative not to linger too long.
Knowing that one cannot remain for long,
one then knows where to act with the swiftness of a rabbit and the suddenness of a duck taking flight, and where to meet life and death.
Even if there are dangerous rivers, cross them;
even if there are great mountains blocking the way, break through them.
Combine one's spirit and concentrate one's essence,
the mind without worry,
the eyes without seeing,
If the ears hear nothing,
then all actions become martial and forceful.
When Ran Shu swore to die for Lord Tian,
the whole state of Qi was afraid.
When Yu Rang swore to die for Xiangzi,
the whole Zhao clan was terrified.
When Cheng Jing devoted himself to death for the Lord of Han,
all the people of Zhou were in awe.
How much more so if a state of ten thousand chariots
has something it is truly committed to?
What enemy could there be?
Before blades are even crossed, victory is already within reach.
The enemy's grief, fear, apprehension, and terror
utterly deplete their spirit and essence.
They are all like frenzied souls,
their form and nature separated.
Walking, they know not where they are going;
running, they know not where they are headed.
Even if they possess dangerous obstacles and strategic passes,
sharp weapons and keen armor,
their hearts dare not rely on them,
their minds dare not settle upon them.
This is how Xia Jie came to die at Nanchao.
Now, if you strike wood with wood, they separate;
if you throw water into water, it scatters;
if you throw ice into ice, it sinks;
if you throw mud into mud, it gets mired.
These are matters of speed, slowness, precedence, and sequence.
Now, warfare has a crucial key.
If one understands strategy and can anticipate what others don't anticipate and prevent what others can't prevent, then one will succeed.
Zhuan Zhu exemplifies this.
He only had to raise his sword with one hand and reach his target,
and the King of Wu achieved his goal.
How much more so with a righteous army!
Whether it's in the tens of thousands,
or just a few thousand,
if you conceal your movements,
and create opportunities for the enemy,
then your soldiers will surely be more effective than Zhuan Zhu himself!
8.3 *Selections*
It says:
It is often said:
"To drive common people into battle can defeat those who have highly paid and well-trained soldiers;
to use the old, weak, and exhausted can defeat those who have elite and skilled troops;
to use the scattered and encumbered can defeat those who have well-ordered formations;
to use hoes and wooden sticks can defeat those who have long halberds and sharp weapons."
This is the argument of someone who doesn't understand warfare.
Suppose you have a sharp sword here,
but if you thrust, you can't hit the mark;
if you strike, you can't reach the target,
then it's no different from a bad sword.
To use a bad sword as a reason for fighting is unacceptable.
Select and choose the finest,
with weapons and equipment being sharp and effective,
but deploying them at the wrong time,
and releasing them inappropriately,
is no different from having bad soldiers.
To use bad soldiers as a reason for fighting is unacceptable.
Prince Qing Ji and Chen Nian still desired the advantage of sharp swords.
Select and choose the finest,
with weapons and equipment being sharp and effective,
and appoint someone capable to lead them.
In ancient times, some achieved kingship, and some achieved hegemony.
Tang, Wu, Duke Huan of Qi, Duke Wen of Jin, and He Lu of Wu are examples of this.
Yin Tang had seventy excellent chariots,
and six thousand men ready to die,
fought at Cheng on the day of Wuzi,
and captured Tuiyi and Daxi.
Ascending from Mingtiao,
he entered the Chao Gate,
and thus possessed the Xia dynasty.
After Jie fled,
he then practiced great benevolence and kindness,
to care for the black-haired people;
reversing the deeds of Jie,
promoting the virtuous and good,
and following what the people liked;
those near and far submitted to him,
Thus, he became king over all under Heaven.
King Wu had three thousand elite Tiger Warriors,
and three hundred selected chariots.
With these, he met the army of Zhou at Muye on the day of Jiazi and captured Zhou as if he were an animal.
He made clear the positions of worthy men,
promoted the remaining elders of the Yin dynasty,
and inquired about the desires of the people.
He bestowed rewards even upon birds and beasts,
and did not avoid punishing even the Son of Heaven,
treated the Yin people as if they were Zhou people,
and regarded others as he regarded himself.
All under Heaven praised his virtue,
and the myriad people rejoiced in his righteousness.
Therefore, he was established as the Son of Heaven.
Duke Huan of Qi had three hundred excellent chariots
and trained ten thousand soldiers
to be the heads of his army.
He rampaged within the seas,
and no one under Heaven was able to stop him.
To the south, he reached Shiliang;
to the west, Feng and Hao;
to the north, Lingzhi.
When Zhongshan destroyed Xing,
and the Di people extinguished Wei,
Duke Huan re-established Xing in Yiyi
and re-established Wei in Chuqiu.
Duke Wen of Jin created five chariots of "five-weight" warriors [each chariot carrying heavily armed soldiers],
and a thousand elite soldiers.
He used these to engage the enemy first.
None of the feudal lords could withstand him.
He overturned the ramparts of Zheng,
and tilled the fields of Eastern Wei.
He honored the Son of Heaven at Hengyong.
King Helü of Wu selected five hundred men of great strength,
and three thousand men with nimble feet [fast runners]
to form the vanguard.
Fighting against Jing,
he won five battles out of five.
Consequently, he possessed Ying.
He campaigned east as far as Bilu,
and west as far as Ba and Shu.
To the north, he pressed upon Qi and Jin,
and his commands were carried out throughout the Central States.
Therefore, regarding the terrain of military power and strategic passes,
the aim is for them to be advantageous.
Regarding armor, weaponry, and equipment,
the aim is for them to be effective.
Regarding selecting, training, and testing martial talents,
the aim is for them to be refined.
Regarding commanding and leading soldiers and people,
the aim is for them to be well-instructed.
These four,
are aids to righteous armies.
They are responses to changing times,
not to be relied upon exclusively because they cannot always be brought about.
These are strategies for victory.
8.4 *Jue Sheng* (Decisive Victory)
Fourth:
Now, armies have fundamental components:
they must have righteousness,
they must have wisdom,
they must have courage.
If righteous, then the enemy is isolated;
if the enemy is isolated, then superiors and inferiors are weak,
and the people are scattered.
Isolation causes fathers and elder brothers to resent,
the worthy to criticize,
and internal disorder to arise.
If wise, then one knows the changes of the times;
knowing the changes of the times, one knows the transformations of emptiness and fullness, waxing and waning,
and knows the calculations of precedence and subsequence, distance and proximity, allowance and abandonment.
If courageous, then one is capable of decisive action;
if capable of decisive action, then one can be like thunder, lightning, whirlwind, and rainstorm,
and can be like collapsing mountains and broken banks, distinctly discerning what falls from the sky.
Like the strike of a fierce bird,
when it seizes its prey it kills it,
and when it strikes a tree it shatters it.
These are obtained through wisdom.
Now, the people have no constant courage,
nor do they have constant cowardice.
If they have spirit (qi), then they are substantial;
if substantial, then courageous.
If they lack spirit, then they are empty;
if empty, then cowardly.
Cowardice and courage, emptiness and substantiality,
their causes are very subtle
and must not be ignored.
Courage leads to battle,
cowardice leads to defeat.
To win in battle
is to fight against the courageous;
to be defeated in battle
is to fight against the cowardly.
Courage and cowardice are inconstant,
fleetingly coming and going,
and none know their direction.
Only the sage alone sees what causes them to be so.
Therefore, the Shang and Zhou dynasties rose,
and Jie and Zhou perished.
The reason why skill and clumsiness surpass each other
is whether one increases the people's spirit or diminishes the people's spirit,
whether one is able to fight as a multitude or is unable to fight as a multitude.
Though the army may be large,
and the soldiers may be many,
it is of no benefit to victory.
If an army has many soldiers but they cannot fight,
the multitude is not as good as a few.
Now, the blessings that come from a large army are great,
but the disasters it brings are also great.
It is like fishing in a deep abyss;
the fish you catch will be large,
but the harm it can cause is also great.
Those skilled in the use of troops
make it so that within the borders,
everyone is involved in the fight.
Even common laborers and ordinary foot soldiers,
from hundreds of *li* away,
all come to join the battle;
the circumstances force them to do so.
The key to good fortune
lies in knowing the date of battle and having a way to restrain and entice them.
Now, in general, troops
value adaptability.
Adaptability means
using the enemy's vulnerabilities to make yourself secure,
and turning the enemy's plans to your own advantage.
If one can understand adaptability and add to it, victory will be inexhaustible.
To have inexhaustible victory is called "divine,"
and being "divine" means being able to avoid defeat.
Now, in warfare,
what is valued is being unbeatable.
Being unbeatable lies in oneself,
being defeatable lies in the enemy.
A sage relies on what is within himself,
and not necessarily on what is in the other.
Therefore, he holds to an invincible strategy to meet a conquerable enemy.
If this is so, then his army will never fail.
All victories in war
are due to the enemy's errors.
The army that wins and the army that loses
must be concealed and subtle,
must accumulate and concentrate.
Concealment overcomes exposure,
subtlety overcomes obviousness,
accumulation overcomes dispersion,
and concentration overcomes separation.
All animals that seize, grab, resist, and bite
using their teeth, horns, claws, and fangs,
must rely on lowness, subtlety, and concealment.
This is how they achieve victory.
8.5 "Loving Gentlemen"
Fifthly:
Clothing people
is because they are cold;
feeding people
is because they are hungry.
Hunger and cold
are the greatest harms to people.
Rescuing them
is a great act of righteousness.
A person's distress and poverty
is as severe as hunger and cold.
Therefore, a wise ruler must pity people's distress
and grieve for their poverty.
If he does so, his reputation will be prominent,
and the worthiest men of the state will be obtained.
In the past, Duke Mu of Qin was riding a carriage when it broke down.
The right-hand horse escaped and was taken by a countryman.
Duke Mu himself went to look for it
and saw the countryman about to eat it on the south side of Mount Qi.
Duke Mu sighed and said,
"Eating the flesh of a fine horse without drinking wine
will harm people. I fear it will harm you!"
So he provided wine for all to drink before they left.
A year later,
in the Battle of Hanyuan,
the Jin people had surrounded Duke Mu's chariot.
Jin generals You Mi of Liang had already seized Duke Mu's left-hand horse,
and Shi Fen, the right-hand officer of Duke Hui of Jin, struck Duke Mu's armor with a spear,
hitting it six times.
The more than three hundred country people who had eaten the horse meat on the south side of Mount Qi all exerted their strength to fight fiercely for Duke Mu under the chariot,
and thus greatly defeated Jin
and captured Duke Hui to bring him back. This is what the *Book of Poetry* means when it says,
"If the ruler treats gentlemen with correctness,
he will practice his virtue;
if the ruler treats commoners with leniency,
they will exhaust their strength for him."
How can a ruler not strive to practice virtue and love his people?
If he practices virtue and loves his people, then the people will be close to their superiors;
if the people are close to their superiors, then they will all gladly die for their ruler.
Zhao Jianzi had two white horses that he loved very much.
Yangcheng Xuqu was in charge of the Guangmen gate.
One night, he knocked on the gate and requested an audience, saying:
"Your subject Xuqu is ill.
The doctor told me:
'If you can obtain the liver of a white horse, the illness will stop;
if you cannot, you will die.'"
The gatekeeper went in to report.
Dong An Yu was attending to Jianzi at his side.
He angrily said:
"Ha!
Xuqu
is scheming to get our lord's horse!
I request that he be immediately punished."
Jianzi said:
"To kill a man to save an animal,
would that not be unbenevolent?
To kill an animal to save a man,
would that not be benevolent?"
Thereupon he summoned the cook to kill the white horse
and take its liver to give to Yangcheng Xuqu.
Not long after,
Zhao raised an army to attack the Di.
The officers of the Guangmen gate,
Seven hundred men on the left,
seven hundred men on the right,
all climbed first and captured armored heads.
How could a ruler not value warriors?
Whenever enemies come,
they come seeking advantage.
Now they come and find death,
meaning they advance without gaining advantage, and even taking flight becomes advantageous.
If all the enemy take flight as advantageous,
then there will be no contact with blades.
Thus, if the enemy gains life from me,
then I will gain death from the enemy.
If the enemy gains death from me,
then I will gain life from the enemy.
To gain life from the enemy,
and for the enemy to gain life from me,
how can we not examine this closely?
This is the essence of warfare.
Survival, destruction, death, and life,
are determined solely by understanding this.
The Records of Late Autumn, Ninth
9.1 "Records of Late Autumn"
It is said:
In the month of Late Autumn:
the sun is in Fang,
at dusk, Xu is in the middle (of the sky),
at dawn, Liu is in the middle (of the sky).
The days are Geng and Xin.
The Emperor is Shao Hao.
The Spirit is Rushou.
The creature is the hairy kind.
The note is Shang.
The musical pipe corresponds to Wushe.
The number is nine.
The taste is acrid.
The smell is rank.
The sacrifice is to the gate.
The first offering is the liver.
Observe the arrival of the geese.
Guest birds enter the great water and become clams.
Chrysanthemums have yellow flowers.
The jackal then sacrifices beasts and slaughters birds.
The Son of Heaven resides in the rightmost chamber of the Zongzhang hall,
rides the war chariot,
yokes white camels,
bears a white flag,
wears white clothes,
adorns himself with white jade,
eats hemp and dog.
The utensils are refined and deep.
In this month,
strictly enforce commands.
Order all officials, noble and base,
to diligently focus on bringing in,
in order to assemble the stored [resources] of Heaven and Earth,
without any being announced or divulged.
He orders the Grand Steward
that the agricultural affairs be completely gathered in,
to select the essentials of the five grains,
and store the collected produce from the Emperor's field in the divine granary, with reverence and utmost care.
In this month,
when frost first begins to descend,
then all the artisans rest.
Thereupon he commands the officials, saying:
"The cold air has completely arrived,
and the strength of the people cannot endure it;
let them all enter their homes."
On the first *ding* day,
he orders the Music Master to begin practicing wind instruments.
In this month,
a great offering is made to the Emperor [Heaven],
and the sacrificial animals are tasted,
reporting the preparations to the Son of Heaven.
He convenes the lords,
and regulates the hundreds of counties.
He prepares for the coming year's reception of the first day of the month, and [establishes] the laws regarding the lightness or heaviness of taxes levied on the people by the lords.
The amount of tribute
is determined according to the distance [from the capital], the land, and what is suitable [for it],
in order to supply the affairs of the suburban altars and ancestral temples,
with nothing taken for personal use.
In this month,
the Son of Heaven then instructs in hunting,
in order to practice with the five weapons.
He conducts a general hunt.
He orders the coachmen and the seven grooms all to harness their horses, to load the pennants and banners onto the carriages,
and to receive their vehicles according to rank.
They are properly arranged outside the screen.
The Minister of Instruction, holding a baton,
faces north to swear them in.
The Son of Heaven then puts on his hunting attire and makes preparations,
holding a bow and grasping arrows to shoot.
He orders the chief sacrificer
to offer sacrifices of game in the four directions.
In this month,
the grasses and trees turn yellow and fall,
and then wood is cut to make charcoal.
Hibernating insects all bow their heads in their burrows,
and all seal up their doors.
Then they expedite legal punishments,
not leaving any who are guilty unpunished.
They collect emoluments and stipends from those who are unworthy, and stop support from those who are not deserving.
In this month,
the Son of Heaven then uses dogs to taste the rice,
and first offers it to the ancestral temple.
If in the final month of autumn summer orders are carried out,
then the country will suffer great floods,
weapons will be stored away, causing disaster and defeat,
and the people will suffer from many nasal congestions and blockages.
If winter orders are carried out,
then the country will have many thieves and bandits,
the borders will not be peaceful,
and the land will be divided.
If spring orders are carried out,
then warm winds will arrive,
the people's spirit will be relaxed and dissolute,
and military campaigns will certainly arise.
9.2 *Following the People*
Second, it says:
The former kings first followed the hearts of the people,
therefore their achievements and fame were established.
Indeed, those who gained the people's hearts through virtue and established great achievements and fame, there were many in ancient times.
Those who lost the people's hearts and established achievements and fame, there has never been such a case.
There must be a way to gain the people,
whether it is a state with ten thousand chariots,
or a town with a hundred households,
the people will have no reason to be displeased.
Take what pleases the people and the people will be taken,
how numerous are the things that please the people?
This is the key to gaining the people.
In the past, Tang conquered Xia and rectified the world,
There was a great drought,
with five years of no harvest.
Tang then used himself to pray in the Mulberry Forest,
saying:
"If I, the one person, am guilty,
do not extend it to the myriad people.
If the myriad people are guilty,
let it rest on me, the one person.
Do not, because of the lack of wisdom of one person,
cause God and the spirits to harm the lives of the people."
Thereupon he cut his hair
and his nails,
using himself as a sacrifice,
to pray for blessings from God.
The people were greatly pleased,
and the rain then came down in abundance.
Thus, Tang understood the transformations of the spirits
and the transmissions of human affairs.
King Wen, dwelling in Qi, served Zhou,
enduring injustice and humiliation with elegance and humility.
Morning and evening he was always punctual,
the tribute he offered was always appropriate,
and sacrifices were always reverent.
Zhou was pleased
and ordered King Wen to be called the Western Overlord,
granting him a thousand li of land.
King Wen bowed his head and kowtowed, declining, saying:
"I wish to request on behalf of the people the punishment of roasting."
King Wen was not averse to a thousand leagues of land,
but requesting the punishment of roasting on behalf of the people was certainly to gain the hearts of the people.
Gaining the hearts of the people is more valuable than a thousand leagues of land,
therefore it is said that King Wen was wise.
King of Yue endured the shame of Kuaiji,
and wished deeply to gain the hearts of the people,
in order to bring about certain death for Wu.
He did not rest comfortably on his pillow,
his mouth did not relish rich flavors,
his eyes did not look upon extravagance,
his ears did not listen to bells and drums.
For three years he toiled with his body and exerted his strength,
parching his lips and drying his lungs.
Inwardly he was close to his officials,
and outwardly he nourished the common people,
in order to draw their hearts to him.
If there were sweet and crisp delicacies insufficient to share,
he would not dare to eat them;
if there was wine, he poured it into the river,
sharing it together with the people.
He personally plowed and ate (what he produced),
his wife personally wove and clothed (herself).
He forbade delicacies,
he forbade layered garments,
he forbade more than two colors.
He would often go out on the roads,
He loaded food into carts,
in order to observe the lonely, widowed, old, weak, those suffering from diseases, the distressed, impoverished, those with worried and gaunt appearances, and those who lacked sustenance.
He personally fed them.
Then he gathered his officials and addressed them,
saying:
"I wish to share with Wu the burden of the world's troubles.
Now the states of Wu and Yue
are mutually destroying each other.
The officers and gentlemen tread on each other's livers and lungs,
dying on the same day.
I wish to grapple with the King of Wu, neck to neck, arm to arm, and fall together. This is my greatest desire.
If this is unattainable,
and I internally assess that my state is insufficient to harm Wu,
and externally I cannot rely on the feudal lords to injure him,
then I will abandon my state,
dismiss my ministers,
wear a sword on my arm,
change my appearance,
alter my name and surname,
and, holding a broom, serve him as a subject,
in order to contend with the King of Wu for one single day of death.
Although I know that my head will not remain attached to my body,
and my head and feet will be in different places,
my four limbs torn apart,
and I will be executed for the world to see,
my will shall surely prevail."
So then, on another day, he indeed fought with Wu at the Five Lakes.
The Wu army was greatly defeated,
Thereupon he greatly besieged the royal palace,
and the city gates were not defended.
He captured Fucha,
executed the Wu chancellor,
and destroyed Wu within two years, achieving hegemony.
This was because he first followed the will of the people.
Duke Zhuang of Qi requested to attack Yue,
and asked Hezi.
Hezi said:
"The former ruler had a testamentary decree saying:
'Do not attack Yue,
Yue is a fierce tiger.'"
Duke Zhuang said:
"Even if it is a fierce tiger,
now it is already dead."
Hezi told this to Xiaozi.
Xiaozi said:
"To consider what is already dead as still living."
Therefore, in all undertakings,
one must first examine the will of the people before one can proceed.
9.3 "Knowing Scholars"
It is said:
Now, suppose there is a horse capable of traveling a thousand li,
unless it finds a skilled craftsman,
it is as if it were not even worth acquiring.
The skilled craftsman and the horse,
Mutual compatibility is required for success.
It is like the drumstick and the drum.
Now, men also have the capacity to travel a thousand *li*;
to uphold high principles and die for righteousness,
this is the capacity of a man to travel a thousand *li*.
That which enables a man to travel a thousand *li*
is only the wise person.
Lord Jingguo was fond of Ji Maobian.
Ji Maobian was a person who was often criticized,
and his disciples did not like him.
An officer tried to prove this to Lord Jingguo,
but Lord Jingguo did not listen,
and the officer resigned and left.
Lord Mengchang secretly advised Lord Jingguo about this,
and Lord Jingguo was greatly angered, saying:
"Eradicate this category!
Considering my household,
if there is something I can do to serve Ji Maobian,
I will not hesitate to do it."
Thereupon, he lodged him in the best quarters,
ordered his eldest son to drive for him,
and served him meals morning and evening.
After several years,
King Wei died,
and King Xuan ascended the throne.
Lord Jingguo's relationship
was greatly disliked by King Xuan.
He resigned and went to Xue,
together with Ji Mao Bian.
He stayed for only a short time.
Ji Mao Bian resigned and left,
requesting to see King Xuan.
Lord Jing Guo said,
"The king dislikes Ying very much.
If you go,
you will surely be put to death."
Ji Mao Bian said,
"I certainly do not seek to live."
He insisted on going,
and Lord Jing Guo could not stop him.
Ji Mao Bian went
and arrived in Qi.
King Xuan heard of it
and concealed his anger to await him.
Ji Mao Bian met King Xuan.
The king said,
"Are you the one whom Lord Jing Guo listens to and loves?"
Ji Mao Bian replied,
"He loves me, that is true,
but he does not listen to me.
When Your Majesty was the Crown Prince,
I said to Lord Jing Guo,
'The Crown Prince's appearance is unbenevolent.
He has an overhanging chin and a pig-like gaze.
Such a person is prone to betrayal.
It would have been better to remove the Crown Prince and
install the infant Xiaoshi, son of Lady Wei.
Lord Jingguo wept and said,
"Impossible,
I cannot bear to do it."
If Lord Jingguo had listened to Bian and acted accordingly,
there would surely not be today's troubles.
This is the first reason.
As for Xue,
Zhao Yang requested to exchange several times the territory for Xue,
and Bian again said,
"You must agree to it."
Lord Jingguo said,
"I received Xue from the late king,
even if it is disliked by the current king,
what would I say to the late king?
Furthermore, the late king's ancestral temple is in Xue,
how could I give the late king's ancestral temple to Chu?"
Again, he would not listen to Bian.
This is the second reason."
King Xuan sighed,
his expression changed,
and said,
"Lord Jingguo was this devoted to me!
I was young
and didn't know this.
Would you, sir, be willing to summon Lord
Jingguo for me?"
Ji Mao Bian replied,
"I respectfully accept."
Lord Jing Guo arrived,
wearing King Wei's clothes,
wearing his crown,
and wearing his sword.
King Xuan personally welcomed Lord Jing Guo in the suburbs,
and wept when he saw him.
Lord Jing Guo arrived,
and was then asked to be prime minister.
Lord Jing Guo declined,
but had no choice but to accept.
After ten days,
he pleaded illness,
strongly declined,
and after three days, he was listened to.
At that time,
Lord Jing Guo can be said to have been able to know people well.
Because he was able to know people well,
criticism did not obstruct him.
This is why Ji Mao Bian outwardly embraced happiness and rushed towards hardship.
9.4 "Examining Oneself"
Fourthly:
Whenever something is the way it is,
there must be a reason.
To know that something is the way it is but not know the reason why,
is the same as not knowing,
Its end will surely be hardship.
The reason why former kings, famous scholars, and accomplished masters surpassed common customs was because of their knowledge.
Water flows from the mountains and runs to the sea.
It is not that water hates the mountains and desires the sea;
the difference in elevation makes it so.
Grain grows in the fields and is stored in the granary;
it is not that grain has desires;
people all make use of it.
Therefore, Zilu covered a pheasant, but then released it.
Master Liezi was learning archery and hit the target.
He inquired about it with Guan Yinzi.
Guan Yinzi said,
"Do you know the reason why you hit the target?"
He answered,
"I do not know."
Guan Yinzi said,
"Not yet."
He withdrew and practiced for three years,
and inquired again.
Guan Yinzi said,
"Do you know the reason why you hit the target?"
Master Liezi said,
"I know it."
Guan Yinzi said,
"It is acceptable.
Guard it and do not lose it."
It is not just archery;
Whether a state exists,
or a state perishes,
whether a person is virtuous,
or a person is unworthy,
all have their reasons.
Therefore, a sage does not examine existence, perishing, virtue, or unworthiness,
but examines the reasons behind them.
Qi attacked Lu,
seeking the Cen tripod.
The Lord of Lu loaded another tripod and sent it.
The Marquis of Qi did not believe it and returned it,
thinking it was not the real one.
He sent someone to tell the Lord of Lu, saying,
"If Liu Xia Ji thinks it is the real one,
please let him confirm it."
The Lord of Lu asked Liu Xia Ji.
Liu Xia Ji replied,
"Your Majesty's bribe
is to obtain the Cen tripod,
and to save the state from destruction.
I also have a state here [within myself].
To destroy my state to save Your Majesty's state,
this is what is difficult for me."
Thereupon, the Lord of Lu then sent the real Cen tripod.
Furthermore, Liu Xia Ji can be said to be skilled in persuasion,
not only preserving his own "state" (integrity),
but also preserving the state of the Lord of Lu.
King Min of Qi, having fled and resided in Wei,
walked on foot during the day,
and said to Gongyu Dan:
"I am already ruined,
but I do not know the reason why.
The reason for my ruin,
what exactly is it?
I should know."
Gongyu Dan replied:
"Your servant thought Your Majesty already knew it,
is it that Your Majesty still does not know?
The reason for Your Majesty's ruin
is because of your virtue.
The kings of the world are all unworthy,
and they hate Your Majesty's virtue,
and therefore joined forces to attack Your Majesty,
this is the reason for Your Majesty's ruin."
King Min sighed deeply and said:
"Is virtue really so bitter?"
This is also not knowing the reason why;
this is why Gongyu Dan was wrong.
The King of Yue had four sons.
The King of Yue's younger brother, named Yu,
wanted to kill them all
and become the successor himself.
He hated three of them and killed them,
The people of the state did not speak well of him,
considering it a great wrong to their ruler.
Furthermore, they detested one particular individual and wished to kill him,
but the King of Yue did not listen to them.
The individual's son, fearing that he would surely die,
seized upon the people's desire to expel Yu,
and surrounded the royal palace.
The King of Yue sighed and said,
"I did not heed Yu's words,
and thus have encountered this difficulty."
He also did not know the reason for his downfall.
9.5 _Proficiency_
Fifth section:
Some say that dodder has no roots.
Dodder is not without roots,
but its root is not attached;
the tuckahoe fungus is its root.
The lodestone attracts iron,
and someone is drawing it.
Trees near each other lean together,
and someone is pushing them.
When a sage faces south and stands,
with the intention of loving and benefiting the people,
even before his commands are issued, the whole world is stretching their necks and raising their heels. That is because he profoundly understands the people.
If one injures others, others will do the same.
Now, those who attack,
Sharpening and whetting the five weapons,
extravagant clothing and delicious food,
the launching of the attack is already scheduled;
those who are to be attacked are not happy.
It is not that someone heard of it;
the spirits foretell it.
One's body is in Qin,
while those one loves are in Qi.
In death, the will and spirit are uneasy;
the essence perhaps wanders back and forth.
Virtue is
the master of the myriad people.
The moon is
the origin of all Yin.
When the moon is full, the clams and shellfish are full,
and all Yin is abundant;
when the moon is dark, the clams and shellfish are empty,
and all Yin is deficient.
Thus, the moon takes form in the sky,
and all Yin transforms in the depths;
the sage takes virtue as his form in himself,
and the four remote regions are all regulated by benevolence.
Yang Youji shot a rhinoceros,
hitting a stone,
and the arrow drank its feathers (penetrated fully),
such was his sincerity towards the rhinoceros.
Bo Le learned to judge horses,
and all he saw were horses.
He was sincere about horses.
The cook Ding of Song loved to butcher oxen.
All he saw were dead oxen;
for three years he did not see living oxen.
He used his knife for nineteen years,
and its edge was like a newly sharpened whetstone.
He followed the natural principles,
and he was sincere about oxen.
Zhong Ziqi heard someone playing a chime at night and felt sorrow. He sent someone to summon the person and asked,
"Why do you play the chime with such sorrow?"
The person replied,
"My father unfortunately killed someone
and could not live.
My mother was allowed to live,
and she makes wine for the government.
I was allowed to live,
and I play the chime for the government.
I have not seen my mother for three years.
Formerly, the She family saw my mother
and estimated the price to redeem her, but I had no wealth,
and my body is inherently owned by the government.
That is why I am sorrowful."
Zhong Ziqi sighed and said,
"Alas!
Alas!
The heart is not an arm,
The arm is not a hammer, nor is it a stone.
Sorrow exists in the heart, and wood and stone respond to it.
Therefore, a gentleman is sincere in this and speaks of that;
he feels it himself and expresses it to others.
Why must he force an explanation?
In the Zhou dynasty, there was a man named Shen Xi.
He lost his mother.
He heard a beggar singing beneath his door and felt sorrow for him,
which was evident in his expression.
He told the gatekeeper to bring the singer in.
He became aware [of the situation] and asked him,
saying:
"Why do you beg?"
He spoke with him,
and [realized] it was his mother.
Therefore, the relationship of parents to children,
and of children to parents,
is one body divided into two,
sharing the same breath with different respiration.
It is like grass and reeds having flowers and fruit,
like trees having roots and a heartwood.
Although in different places, they communicate with each other,
hidden intentions reach each other,
pain and illness are mutually relieved,
worries and thoughts are mutually felt,
in life they rejoice together,
in death they grieve together.
This is what is meant by the closeness of flesh and blood.
Spirit emerges from loyalty,
and responds to the heart.
When two essences obtain each other,
how can it wait for words?
Chapter Ten, The Record of Early Winter
10.1 *The Record of Early Winter*
It says:
In the month of early winter:
The sun is in Tail;
At dusk, 危 (Wei) is in the middle;
At dawn, the Seven Stars are in the middle.
Its days are Ren and Gui.
Its Emperor is Zhuanxu.
Its God is Xuanming.
Its insect is shelled.
Its note is Yu.
The musical pipe resonates with Yingzhong.
Its number is six.
Its taste is salty.
Its odor is rotten.
Its sacrifice is Xing.
Offer sacrifice first to the kidneys.
Water begins to ice over;
The earth begins to freeze.
Pheasants enter the great water and become蜃 (shen, a kind of shellfish).
Rainbows hide and are not seen.
The Son of Heaven dwells in the left compartment of the Dark Hall,
Ride in a black carriage,
drawn by iron-black horses,
bearing black banners,
wear black clothing,
adorn oneself with black jade,
eat millet and pork.
The vessels used are large and covered.
In this month,
winter begins.
Three days before the beginning of winter,
the Grand Scribe informs the Son of Heaven,
saying:
"On such and such day, winter begins,
and the flourishing virtue resides in Water."
The Son of Heaven then fasts.
On the day of the beginning of winter,
the Son of Heaven personally leads the Three Dukes, Nine Ministers, and Great Officers to welcome winter in the northern suburbs.
Upon returning, he rewards those who died in service
and provides for orphans and widows.
In this month,
the Grand Diviner is ordered
to pray and sacrifice to the tortoise shells and milfoil stalks to divine auspicious and inauspicious omens,
and to carefully examine the prognostication's good and bad fortunes.
Hereupon, examine those who flatter and disobey the law and punish them, without any concealment.
In this month,
The Son of Heaven begins to wear furs.
He commands the officials, saying:
"The air of Heaven ascends,
the air of Earth descends,
Heaven and Earth do not communicate,
closing up to become winter."
He orders the hundred officials
to carefully cover and store away.
He orders the Minister of Education
to inspect accumulated stores,
He strengthens the city walls,
takes precautions at the gates,
repairs bolts and locks,
is careful with keys and bolts,
secures seals,
prepares the borders,
reinforces strategic passes,
is careful with bridges,
blocks narrow paths,
regulates mourning rites,
distinguishes clothing,
examines the thickness of coffins and the size, height, thickness, and depth of burial mounds, according to the rank of the noble and base.
In this month,
he commands the artisans to display their work.
He presents sacrificial vessels,
examines the measures and standards,
ensuring no one creates extravagant and ingenious things
to distract the ruler's mind;
the highest priority must be placed on functional achievement.
Objects are inscribed with the artisan's name
to examine their sincerity;
if the work is improper,
they must be punished
to investigate the circumstances fully.
Hibernating creatures re-emerge.
If one carries out autumnal decrees,
then snow and frost will be untimely,
small-scale warfare will arise frequently,
and territory will be encroached upon and diminished.
10.2 *Frugality in Funerals*
Secondly, it is said:
To thoroughly understand life is the essence for a sage;
to thoroughly understand death is the ultimate achievement for a sage.
To understand life is
to not harm life with material things,
this is called nurturing life;
to understand death is
to not harm the dead with material things,
this is called setting the dead at peace.
These two things
are what only a sage can decisively determine.
All those who live between Heaven and Earth
are certain to die.
This is unavoidable.
A filial son's regard for his parents,
and a loving parent's affection for their child,
is a pain felt in the very flesh and bone;
it is innate.
To take that which is so highly regarded and so dearly loved,
and abandon it in a ditch or gully after death,
That which was valued and loved,
when dead, is cast away into a ditch.
Human feelings cannot bear to do this,
therefore there is the meaning of burying the dead.
Burying,
is hiding.
It is what kind parents and filial children are careful about.
Being careful about it
is to consider it with the heart of the living.
To consider for the dead with the heart of the living,
nothing is better than not moving the body,
nothing is better than not exhuming it.
Not exhuming and not moving,
nothing is better than having nothing that can be profited from.
Having nothing that can be profited from, this is called secure closure.
In ancient times, there were those who buried in open fields and deep mountains and found peace.
This did not involve pearls, jade, or national treasures.
Burial cannot be without hiding.
If the burial is shallow, then foxes and wildcats will dig it up;
if it is deep, then it will reach the water and springs.
Therefore, all burials must be on high mounds,
in order to avoid the trouble of foxes and wildcats, and the dampness of water and springs.
This is good,
but to forget the trouble of treachery, evil, thieves, robbers, and rebellions,
is it not a delusion?
It is like a blind master avoiding a pillar, avoiding the pillar only to quickly bump into a stake.
The trouble of foxes, wildcats, water, springs, treachery, evil, thieves, robbers, and rebellions,
This is the largest of such stakes.
The benevolent parent and filial son who avoid them
understand the true sentiment of burial.
Good coffins and outer coffins
are to avoid ants, snakes, and insects.
Now, the lords of the greatly disordered world
increasingly extravagantly
embellish their burials; their hearts are not truly considering the deceased,
but the living use it to show off and compete.
The extravagant deem it honorable,
and the frugal deem it crude.
They do not take benefiting the dead as their purpose,
but merely take the praise and criticism of the living as their business.
This is not the heart of a benevolent parent or filial son.
Even though the father is dead,
the filial son's respect for him does not diminish;
even though the son is dead,
the benevolent parent's love for him does not slacken.
If the beloved and respected is buried
according to what the living greatly desire,
how can that bring them peace?
How can it be done?
When it comes to profit, people
brave flying arrows,
tread on bare blades,
and wade through blood to lick livers to obtain it.
Even uncultured people
are willing to harm relatives, brothers, and close friends in order to seek profit.
Now there is no such danger,
no such disgrace.
The profit from it is very great:
riding in carriages and eating meat,
the benefit extending to sons and grandsons.
Even sages could not prohibit it,
how much less a time of disorder?
The state becomes larger,
the family becomes richer,
and the burial becomes more extravagant.
Pearls are placed in the mouth and scales (of fish) are arranged (around the body); pearls, jade, playthings, and precious goods,
bells, tripods, and ewers overflowing (the tomb);
carriages, horses, clothing, blankets, spears, and swords,
cannot be counted completely.
All kinds of things to nourish the living
without exception, follow (the dead).
Log-cabin style chambers,
coffins and outer coffins in many layers,
piled stones and piled charcoal
surround the outside.
Dishonest people hear of it
and spread the word to each other.
Even though the ruler prohibits it with strict authority and heavy penalties,
it still cannot be stopped.
Moreover, the longer the dead have been buried,
the more distant the living become;
the more distant the living become,
the more negligent the guards become;
If the guards become increasingly negligent while the burial objects remain as before, the situation is inherently unstable.
In the common customs of funerals,
the coffin is carried on a large platform.
Feathered plumes and banners, like clouds of fans, oversee it; pearls and jade are used to furnish it;
elaborate embroidery and patterns adorn it;
tens of thousands of people pull the ropes on the left and right to move it,
establishing it as if it were a military formation is then acceptable.
Viewing the world in this way,
it is beautiful and extravagant;
but to do this for the dead,
is unacceptable.
If it were beneficial to the dead,
then even if it impoverished the country and exhausted the people,
filial sons and daughters would not hesitate to do it.
10.3 *An Die* (Peaceful Death)
Thirdly:
In the world's construction of burial mounds,
they are as tall and large as mountains,
the trees planted on them are like forests,
the setting up of watchtowers and courtyards, the construction of palaces and the making of guest halls is like a city;
using this to show wealth to the world is acceptable, but to do this for the dead is unacceptable.
For the dead,
their view of ten thousand years is like a single blink of an eye.
A person's lifespan,
even if long, does not exceed a hundred years,
and a moderate lifespan does not exceed sixty years.
To use a hundred or sixty years to plan for the endless future, their feelings must not correspond.
To endlessly worry about the dead is
to grasp at something.
Now, suppose there is a person here
who places a stone inscription on a grave mound,
saying:
"The things inside this [grave],
contain many pearls, jades, playthings, valuables, treasures, and precious vessels.
It is imperative to dig it up;
digging it up will surely bring great wealth,
allowing descendants to ride in carriages and eat meat for generations."
People would surely laugh at this together,
considering it a great delusion.
Extravagant burials in the world are similar to this.
From ancient times to the present,
there has never been a country that has not fallen;
if there is no country that does not fall,
then there is no tomb that is not dug up.
Based on what our ears and eyes have heard and seen,
Qi, Jing, and Yan have already fallen,
Song and Zhongshan have already fallen,
Zhao, Wei, and Han have all fallen;
they are all former states.
The number of fallen states before these is countless,
therefore, there is no ancient grand tomb that is not dug up.
Yet the world all compete to do this [extravagant burials],
is this not lamentable?
A ruler who does not command his people,
Sons who are unfilial to their fathers,
and younger brothers who are not respectful to their elder brothers,
are all those whom the village despises and expels.
Being averse to the labor of plowing and harvesting, gathering firewood,
and unwilling to engage in official duties,
yet desiring the pleasures of fine clothes and extravagant food,
their cleverness and skills become exhausted,
and they have no means to achieve it.
Therefore, they gather crowds of followers
in deep mountains, vast marshes, and forests,
ambushing, attacking, and seizing.
Moreover, they target renowned hills and large tombs with opulent burials,
seeking abandoned places to dwell in,
and secretly excavating them,
day and night without rest,
determined to obtain profit,
which they then divide among themselves.

Now, if one has something loved and valued, yet allows wicked, villainous, thieving, and rebellious people to ultimately disgrace it, this is a matter of great importance for a filial son, a loyal minister, a loving father, and a true friend.
Yao was buried in the Valley Forest,
with a common tree planted;
Shun was buried in Jishi,
where the market never changed its shops;
Yu was buried in Kuaiji,
without troubling laborers;
therefore, the former kings practiced frugality and moderation in burial,
not because they begrudged the expense,
nor because they disliked the labor,
but for the sake of the dead.
What the former kings detested most
was the dishonoring of the dead.
To exhume a body invariably brings dishonor;
frugality prevents exhumation.
Therefore, the burials of the former kings
were necessarily frugal, necessarily conforming, and necessarily uniform.
What does "conforming" mean?
What does "uniform" mean?
To bury in the mountains and forests is to conform to the mountains and forests;
to bury on slopes and wetlands is to be uniform with slopes and wetlands.
This is what is meant by cherishing the dead.
Those who cherish the dead are many,
but those who know how to cherish the living are few.
Therefore, before Song was destroyed, the tombs in the east were plundered;
before Qi was destroyed, the tomb of Duke Zhuang was plundered.
When the state is peaceful and secure, it is still like this,
how much more so after a hundred generations when the state is already destroyed?
Therefore, filial sons, loyal ministers, affectionate fathers, and loyal friends cannot but pay close attention to this.
To love them but instead harm them, to secure them but instead endanger them,
this is what I am talking about.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"One dares not attack a tiger with bare hands,
nor dares one ford the river without a boat.
People know one aspect of this,
but none knows the other."
This speaks of not understanding the neighbors.
Therefore, they turn to opposing each other,
But instead, they use it to affirm each other.
What they criticize is precisely what they affirm,
and what they affirm is precisely what they criticize.
Right and wrong are not yet determined,
yet joy and anger contend and strive,
and are put to use instead.
I do not criticize contention, I do not criticize striving,
but I criticize the reasons for contending, the reasons for striving.
Therefore, all those who contend and strive
do so because right and wrong have already been determined.
Now, many do not first determine what is right and wrong but instead are quick to contend and strive;
this is the greatest of confusions.
When the Lu minister Ji Sun had a funeral,

He entered the gate and turned left,
taking the position of a guest.
The host used jade to receive him (as a gift),
Confucius strode directly through the courtyard and hastened,
climbing the steps,
and said:
"To use precious jade for collection

Strolling directly through the courtyard and climbing the steps
is not in accordance with ritual;
however, it was done to correct an excess.
10.4 *Different Treasures*
Fourthly:
It is not that the people of ancient times had no treasures,
but what they treasured was different.
When Sun Shu'ao was ill

What can be held for a long time
is only this."
Sun Shu'ao died,
and the king indeed offered his son a rich land as a fief.
But the son declined
and requested to have Sleeping Hill.

Sun Shu'ao's wisdom
lay in knowing to consider disadvantage as advantage,
and knowing to take what others dislike as his own joy.
This is why those who possess the Way differ from the common people.
Wu Yuan fled.
Jing (Chǔ) urgently sought him. He ascended Mount Taihang and looked towards Zheng, saying:
"This is the state of Zheng.

not worth undertaking anything with."

He met Duke Xu and asked him where he should go.

but faced southeast and spat.
Wu Yuan repeatedly bowed and accepted the "gift," saying:

Passing through Jing (Chǔ),

In the past, when Wu Zixu passed by,

Why would I now accept your thousand-gold sword?"
Wu Yuan (Zixu) passed by Wu.
He sent people to search for him on the river, but they could not find him. Every time he ate, he would offer a sacrifice to him,
praying:
"Old man on the river!
Heaven and earth are extremely vast,
extremely numerous.
Is there anything that they cannot do?
Yet they do nothing.
They act, yet do nothing for it.

your body cannot be seen.
Is it not you, the old man on the river?"
A villager from Song,
plowing his field, found a jade.
He offered it to Sicheng Zihan,
but Zihan did not accept it.
The villager pleaded:
"This is the treasure of a villager.
I hope that the prime minister will bestow it as a gift and accept it."
Zihan said:
"You consider jade as treasure,

Therefore, an elder of the Song state said:
"It is not that Zihan has no treasures,
