Now, if one presents a hundred gold coins and a handful of millet to a child,
Tang and Wu employed their talents and thus achieved their kingship.
Tang saw a net-setter,
who had set up nets on all four sides.
His prayer was:
"Those who fall from the sky,
those who emerge from the earth,
those who come from the four directions,
may all enter my net."
Tang said:
"Alas!
He is taking everything.
If not Jie, who else would do this?"
Tang removed three sides of the net,
set up one side,
and changed the prayer, saying:

Those who wish to go left, go left,
those who wish to go right, go right,
those who wish to go high, go high,
those who wish to go low, go low,
I will only take those who violate my commands."
The state of Hannan heard of this and said:
"Tang's virtue extends even to birds and beasts."
Forty states submitted to him.
If someone sets up nets on four sides,
they may not necessarily catch a bird;
Tang removed three sides [of the net],
leaving one side,
to net his forty states;
it wasn't merely netting birds.
King Wen of Zhou had people dig a pond,
[and they] obtained the bones of a dead person.
An official reported this to King Wen.
King Wen said,
"Rebury them."
The official said,
"These have no owner."
King Wen said,
"He who possesses all under Heaven,
is the master of all under Heaven;
he who possesses a state,
is the master of that state.
Am I not their master?"
Thereupon he ordered the official to rebury them with a coffin and clothes.
The world heard of this and said,
"King Wen is virtuous,
his benevolence extends to bones,
how much more so to people?"
Someone might obtain a treasure and endanger their state,
King Wen obtained rotten bones and used them to convey his meaning,
therefore, for the sage, there is nothing among things that is not useful.
When Confucius' disciples came from afar,
Confucius, carrying a staff, inquired of him, saying:
"Is your lord not unwell?"
He grasped his staff and greeted him,
asking:
"Are your parents not unwell?"
He put down his staff and asked:
"Are your brothers not unwell?"
He took a short step and doubled it,
asking:
"Is your wife not unwell?"
Therefore, Confucius, with a six-foot staff,
elucidated the distinctions of nobility and baseness,
and distinguished the meaning of closeness and distance in relationships.
How much more so with high positions and generous emoluments?
In ancient times, people valued skill in archery
to support the elderly and nurture the young.
Nowadays, people value skill in archery
for attacking, fighting, invading, and seizing.
The lesser among them use it to rob the weak and tyrannize the few,
making the aim to obstruct and seize.
When benevolent people obtain sweets,
they use them to nourish the sick and support the aged.
When Zhi and Qiao obtain sweets,

The Eleventh Section, Mid-Winter
11.1 *Zhong Dong Ji* (Annals of Mid-Winter)
First:
The month of mid-winter:
the sun is in Dou (Sagittarius);
at dusk, the Eastern Wall (of Pegasus and Pisces) is in the meridian;
at dawn, Zhen (Corvus) is in the meridian.
Its days are Ren and Gui.
Its deity is Zhuanxu.
Its spirit is Xuanming.
Its creature is shelled.
Its note is Yu.
The standard pitch corresponds to Huangzhong.
Its number is six.
Its taste is salty.
Its smell is rotten.
Its sacrifice is Xing.
The first sacrifice is to the kidneys.
The ice becomes thicker.
The earth begins to crack.
The hedan bird ceases to sing.
Tigers begin to mate.
The Son of Heaven dwells in the Dark Hall of the Great Temple,
rides in a dark carriage,
drawn by iron-black horses,
bearing a dark flag,
wearing black clothes,
adorned with dark jade,
eating millet with pork.
Its utensils are large and covered.
He commands the officials, saying:
"Do not undertake earthworks,
do not open storehouses,
do not raise large crowds,
in order to secure Heaven's closure of the earth."
To open storehouses,
to raise large crowds,
The pottery must be good,
the fire kindling must be obtained,
and all six materials must be used together.
A high-ranking official oversees it,
so there are no errors.
The Son of Heaven then commands the officials
to pray and sacrifice to the four seas, great rivers, famous plains, deep pools, and wells and springs.
In this month,
if there are farmers who do not store and gather crops,
or cattle, horses, and livestock that have been let loose and strayed,
they may be taken without question.
In the mountains, forests, and marshes,
if there are those who can gather coarse food, hunt, or capture birds and beasts,
the gamekeepers will instruct and guide them;
those who encroach upon and seize from each other
will be punished without pardon.
In this month,
the winter solstice arrives.
Yin and Yang contend,
and all living things are agitated.
The ruler fasts and purifies himself,
and his dwelling must be well-protected.
His body desires tranquility,
so he avoids music and sensual pleasure,
and forbids excessive desires.
He rests his body and mind,
Affairs should be kept still,
in order to await the determination of Yin and Yang.
Rue begins to sprout.
*Liting* grass emerges.
Earthworms knot together.
Elk antlers fall off.
Springs begin to flow.
When the days reach their shortest,
then fell forest trees
and gather bamboo arrows.
In this month,
those officials who have no duties can be dismissed,
and useless tools can be discarded.
Plaster the watchtowers, the courtyard gates, and the outer gates;
build prisons.
This is how to assist Heaven and Earth in their process of closing and storing.
If in mid-winter the commands of summer are carried out,
then the country will experience drought,
the air will be misty and gloomy,
and thunder will sound.
If the commands of autumn are carried out,
then the weather will bring heavy rain,
gourds will not ripen,
and the country will have great armies.
If the commands of spring are carried out,
then insects will cause damage,
When springs and fountains diminish and dry up,
the people will suffer many illnesses and plagues.
11.2 "Utmost Loyalty"
It is said:
Utmost loyal words grate upon the ear and upset the heart.
If not a virtuous ruler, who could bear to listen to them?
Therefore, what a virtuous ruler delights in
is what an unworthy ruler punishes.
No ruler does not hate those who are violent and plundering,
yet they daily bring them about.
What good does hating them do?
Now, if there is a tree here,
and one desires it to be beautiful,
yet someone waters it only occasionally,
then he hates it,
and then he chops at its roots himself,
then there will certainly be no living tree.
To hate hearing loyal words
is to chop at one's own vital essence.
King Zhuang'ai of Jing hunted in Yunmeng.
He shot a rhinoceros,
hitting it.
Shen Gongzi Pei seized the king and snatched it away.
The king said,
"How violent and disrespectful!"
He was about to order the officers to execute him.
The courtiers and grandees all stepped forward to advise him, saying,
"Gongzi Pei
is a worthy man,
and he is a minister a hundred times greater than others to the king.
There must be a reason for this.
We wish that the king would examine it further."
In less than three months,
Zi Pei fell ill and died.
The Chu state raised an army
and fought against Jin at Liangtang,
achieving a great victory over Jin.
Returning, they rewarded those who had contributed to the victory.
Shen Gongzi Pei's younger brother stepped forward and requested a reward from the officers, saying, "People's merits are achieved in the military campaigns,

Ji Dong Ji Twelfth
12.1 *Ji Dong Ji*
It says:
In the month of Ji Dong (late winter):
the sun is in Wunv (Aquarius),
at dusk, Lou (Pleiades) is in the middle,
at dawn, Di (Libra) is in the middle.
Its days are Ren and Gui.
At the end of the year, perform the ritual of driving away pestilence.
Bring forth the earthen ox
to expel the cold air.
The migratory birds become swift and urgent.
Then, complete the sacrifices to the mountains and rivers,
as well as the great ministers of the sovereign and the deities of heaven and earth.
In this month,
order the fishermen to begin fishing,
and the Son of Heaven goes there in person.
Then, taste the fish,
first offering it in the ancestral temple.
The ice is at its thickest,
and the waters and marshes are frozen solid.
Order the gathering of ice.
Once the ice has been brought in,
instruct officials to inform the people
to bring forth the five kinds of grains.
Order the Minister of Agriculture
to plan the matter of plowing in pairs,
repair plows and hoes,
and prepare farming implements.
Order the music master
to conduct a grand ensemble of wind instruments, then conclude.
Then, order the four supervisors
to collect and classify firewood and brushwood
to supply the ancestral temple and fuel for the bonfires of the various sacrifices.
In this month,
the sun reaches its limit in its station,
the moon reaches its limit in its cycle,
the stars revolve in the heavens,
the count will nearly end,
the year will be renewed,
and concentrate on agriculture,
the people have nothing else to do.
The Son of Heaven, together with the high officials and great officers, then puts in order the national regulations,
discusses the seasonal ordinances,
in order to prepare for the suitability of the coming year.
Then he orders the Grand Historian
to rank the feudal lords,
and assess their sacrificial animals,
in order to supply the offerings to August Heaven, Supreme God, and the altars of the land and grain.
Then he orders the states of the same surname
to supply the grass-fed animals for the ancestral temples.
He orders the stewards to count the number of fields of the high officials, great officers, and even the common people, and assess their sacrificial animals,
in order to supply the sacrifices to the mountains, forests, famous rivers, and streams.

All the people within the nine provinces of the world must all contribute their strength to supply the offerings to August Heaven, Supreme God, the altars of the land and grain, the ancestral temples, mountains, forests, famous rivers, and streams.
Carrying out this ordinance
is called one complete cycle,
thirty-two days.
If in the last month of winter, the ordinances of autumn are carried out,
then the white dew will descend early,
armored insects will become monstrous,
and the four neighboring regions will enter into defense.
If spring decrees are implemented
then there will be many stillbirths and injuries,
and the country will have many chronic illnesses.
This is called being contrary.
If summer decrees are implemented
then floods will ruin the country,
snow will not fall in season,
and ice will melt and dissipate.

Third principle:

12.4 *Honesty and Integrity*
Fourthly:

the rulers of ten thousand chariots,

was nothing more than worthiness.
20.5 《Reaching Stagnation》
It is said fifthly:
Generally, a person has three hundred and sixty joints,
nine orifices, five viscera, and six entrails.
The flesh and skin should be close together,
the blood vessels should be unobstructed,
the muscles and bones should be strong,
the heart and will should be harmonious,
the essence and qi should flow,
if this is so, then illness will have no place to reside and evil will have no way to be born.
The retention of illness and the birth of evil
is due to the stagnation of essence and qi.
Therefore, when water stagnates, it becomes polluted,
when a tree stagnates, it becomes infested with worms,
when grass stagnates, it becomes a (basket) infestation.
A state also has stagnation.
(If) the ruler's virtue does not flow,
and the people's desires are not communicated,
this is the state's stagnation.
If the state's stagnation persists for a long time,
then all kinds of evils arise together,
and myriad disasters spring up in clusters.
The mutual resentment between those above and those below
arises from this.
Therefore, wise kings value brave men and loyal ministers,
because they dare to speak directly and break through the stagnation.
King Lì of Zhōu oppressed the people,
and the people of the state all criticized him.
Shào Gōng reported this to the king, saying:
"The people cannot bear the commands anymore."
The king sent a sorcerer from Wèi to monitor those who criticized him,
and if they were caught, they were killed.
The people of the state dared not speak,
but exchanged glances on the roads.
The king was pleased
and told Shào Gōng, saying:
"I have been able to stop the criticism."
Shào Gōng said:
"This is blocking it,
not stopping it.
Blocking the mouths of the people
More severe than preventing a river from flooding;
if a river is blocked and bursts,
it will certainly destroy many people.
The people are just like that.
Therefore, those who govern rivers unblock them and guide them;
those who govern the people disseminate [information] and allow them to speak.
Therefore, when the Son of Heaven listens to the government,
he has dukes, ministers, and officials offer direct remonstrance,
those who love learning and are widely knowledgeable present poems,
blind admonishers chant,
commoners spread words,
close ministers exhaust their advice,
and relatives supplement observations.
Only then does the King deliberate.
Therefore, the bottom has no overlooked good,
and the top has no excessive actions.
Now the King blocks the mouths of those below,
and thus continues the mistakes of those above,
I fear this will bring worry to the state."
The King did not listen.
Three years later,
the people exiled the King to Zhì 彘.
This was the failure of 鬱 (Yù).
Yù (鬱)
means "not open."
On the Zhōu 周 bronze tripod was depicted a rat,
and a horse was made to trample on it,
because it was "not open."
"Not open"
is a custom of a country that is perishing.
Guǎn Zhòng 管仲 offered wine to Duke Huán 桓 of Qí 齊.
He said, "It is getting late,"
Duke Huán 桓 enjoyed it and requested candles.
Guǎn Zhòng said:
"Your servant divined for the daytime,
but not for the night.
Your lord may leave now."
The Duke was displeased,
saying:
"Zhòng fǔ is old,
how much longer will I be able to enjoy myself with Zhòng fǔ?
Let us please continue the night."
Guǎn Zhòng said:
"Your Lordship is mistaken.
Those who indulge heavily in flavors neglect virtue;
those who are immersed in pleasure revert to sorrow;
if one is lazy when strong, one loses the opportune time;
if one slackens when old, one will have no reputation.
Your servant will now strive on your behalf,
how can you immerse yourself in wine?"
Guǎn Zhòng can be said to have been capable of establishing proper conduct.
Generally, conduct is ruined by indulgence in pleasure,
now, even while enjoying pleasure, he becomes even more disciplined;
conduct is corrupted by noble status,
now, the lord desires to stay, but he does not permit it.
To extend one's will and carry out principles,
to value music and not change because of it,
and thereby serve one's lord;
this is how Duke Huan achieved hegemony.
Liè Jīng Zǐgāo was listened to and employed by King Mǐn of Qí.
He liked to wear eastern cloth garments,
a white silk hat,
and straw sandals.
Once, meeting morning rain, he lifted his clothes and walked down the hall,
and said to his attendants:
"How am I?"
The attendant said:
"You are handsome and beautiful, sir."
Thereupon, Liè Jīng Zǐgāo walked and peered into a well.
He saw the clear image of an ugly man
and sighed and said:
"The attendant wants me to be listened to and employed by the King of Qí,
so how flattering he is!
Moreover, one who is listened to and employed by the lord of ten thousand chariots
is flattered even more.
Yet, without anything to reflect upon himself,
his ruin and destruction will not be far off.
Who should he use as a mirror?
Surely it is a scholar!
Everyone knows to like a mirror for showing their appearance,
but hates a scholar for showing their character.
The merit of a mirror in showing one's appearance is small,
A scholar's understanding of himself is a great accomplishment.
To grasp the small,
and lose the big,
is simply not understanding categories.”
Zhào Jiǎnzǐ said:
“Jué loves me,
Tuó does not love me.
When Jué admonishes me,
it is always in a place where there are no people;
when Tuó admonishes me,
he likes to confront me among the people,
invariably making me look bad.”
Yǐn Tuó replied:
“Jué loves the lord's embarrassment,
but does not love the lord's faults;
Tuó loves the lord's faults,
but does not love the lord's embarrassment.
Your servant has often heard that in selecting men from the multitude,
those with a sincere face and an earthy complexion can endure shame.
Not confronting the lord among the people
is out of fear that the lord would not change."
This shows Jiǎnzǐ’s virtue.
When a ruler is virtuous, his subjects’ words are impactful.
Jiǎnzǐ was not virtuous,
and Tuó ultimately did not reside in the land of Zhào;
how could he be beside Jiǎnzǐ?
20.6 "Conduct and Discourse"
Six said:
The actions of a ruler are different from those of a commoner.
When the situation is unfavorable,
and the timing is not advantageous,
he must treat his enemies with consideration in order to survive.
Holding the lives of the people,
holding the lives of the people,
is a heavy responsibility,
and he must not act solely to satisfy his own desires.
Therefore, if a commoner were to act in this way,
he would be pointed at by the state
and not be tolerated even in his own village.
Yáo ceded the empire to Shùn.
Gǔn, as a feudal lord,
was angry with Yáo and said:
"He who attains the Way of Heaven becomes Emperor,
and he who attains the Way of Earth becomes one of the Three Dukes.
Now I have attained the Way of Earth,
yet you do not make me one of the Three Dukes."
He considered Yáo to have erred in his judgment.
He desired to become one of the Three Dukes.
He was (extremely) angry with his ferocious beasts,
and wanted to use them to create chaos.
If their horns were aligned,
they could form a city;
if their tails were raised,
could be used as a banner.
He was summoned but did not come,
wandering in the wilderness to trouble the emperor.
Therefore, Shùn executed him at Mount Yǔ,
and cut him in half with a Wú knife.
Yǔ did not dare to resent this,
but instead served him,
was appointed as Minister of Public Works,
to clear the floods,
his face was dark,
his steps were not coordinated,
his nasal passages were blocked,
and he won the emperor's heart.
In the past, Zhòu acted without virtue,
killing Méibó and turning him into mincemeat,
killing Guǐhóu and turning him into dried meat,
to show off his power to the feudal lords at the ancestral temple.
King Wén wept and sighed about this.
Zhòu feared that he would rebel,
and wanted to kill King Wén and destroy Zhōu.
King Wén said:
"Even though my father is without virtue,
how could a son dare not serve his father?
Even though the ruler is not benevolent,
how could a minister dare not serve his ruler?
Which king is it permissible to rebel against?"
Zhòu then pardoned him.
The world heard of it and
considered King Wén to be one who feared his superiors and pitied his inferiors.
The "Book of Songs" says:
"Only this King Wén,
was cautiously attentive,
clearly serving God,
and earnestly receiving many blessings."
When Qí attacked Sòng,
the King of Yān sent Zhāng Kuí to lead Yān soldiers to accompany them.
The King of Qí killed him.
The King of Yān heard of it,
tears streamed down his face,
summoned the officials and told them:
"I raise an army, and Qí kills my envoy.
I ask that you order the raising of troops to attack Qí."
He ordered that the command be carried out.
Fán Yáo came to see him,
and argued against it, saying:
"The worthy king formerly wished to be a subject.
Now the king is not a worthy ruler,
I wish to resign from being a subject."
King Zhāo said:
"What is this about?"
He replied:
"During the turmoil at Sōngxià,
the former ruler abandoned his subjects out of unease.
The king endures the pain and serves Qí because
Now that Kuí is dead and the king attacks Qí,
it is regarding Kuí as more worthy than the former ruler."
The king said:
"Yes."
"I ask that the king stop the army."
The king said:
"If so, then what should be done?"
Fán Yáo replied:
"I request that the king wear white mourning clothes and withdraw to a lodge in the suburbs,
and send an envoy to Qí,
to apologize to them as a guest,
saying:
'This is entirely my fault.
The Great King is a virtuous ruler,
how could you kill all the envoys from the lords?
Yet, the envoy from Yàn alone died;
this is because our humble state was not careful in selecting people.
I wish to make amends and beg for forgiveness.'"
The envoy traveled to Qí.
The King of Qí was drinking heavily,
his officials on the left and right were numerous,
and his attendants were very many.
Consequently, he ordered the envoy to advance and report.
The envoy reported that the King of Yàn was greatly fearful and begging for forgiveness.
When finished,
he repeated it again,
to impress the numerous officials on the left and right.
Thereupon, he dispatched a minor envoy to deliver a return order for the King of Yàn to return to the lodge.
This is why (the army at) Jǐ Shàng was defeated,
and the state of Qí was weakened.
(With) seventy cities,
if not for Tián Dān's perseverance, they almost would not have been recovered.
King Mǐn relied on the greatness of Qí and became cruel,
and Tián Dān established merit with the city of Jímò.
The Book of Poetry says:
"If you wish to destroy something,
you must first burden it greatly;
if you wish to overturn something,
you must first raise it high."
his strength is insufficient.
Is this not what it means?
To be burdened and yet not destroyed,
to be raised high and yet not overturned,
that can only be achieved by one who possesses the Dao!
King Zhuāng of Chǔ (楚莊王) sent Wén Wúwèi (文無畏) to Qí (齊).
He passed through Sòng (宋)
without first requesting permission to pass through.
Upon his return,
Huá Yuán (華元) said to Duke Zhāo of Sòng (宋昭公):
"He did not ask permission to pass on his way there,
nor did he ask permission to pass on his way back,
he considers Sòng (宋) to be a wild and rustic place.
During Chǔ's (楚) great hunt,
they whipped your servant at Mèngzhū (孟諸).
I request that he be executed."
Thereupon, he killed Wén Wúwèi (文無畏) at the embankment of Yángliáng (揚梁).
King Zhuāng (莊王) was in the midst of trimming his sleeve,
when he heard of it and exclaimed:
"Alas!"
He threw down his sleeve and rose to his feet,
his shoes reached the courtyard,
his sword reached the gates,
his chariot reached the market of Púshū (蒲䟽),
Some heard this and spread the word, saying:
"The Dīng family, by digging a well, has obtained one person."
The people of the state talked about it.
It reached the ears of the ruler of Sòng.
The ruler of Sòng ordered someone to ask the Dīng family about it.
The Dīng family replied:
"We gained the use of one man's labor,
not that we got a man from within the well."
To seek ability like this
is not as good as not hearing about it at all.
Zǐ Xià (子夏) was going to Jìn (晉),
passing through Wèi (衛).
There was a historiographer reading, saying:
"The Jìn army crossed the river with three pigs."
Zǐ Xià said:
"That is not right,
it is *jǐ hài* (己亥)."
"The character *jǐ* (己) and 'three' (三) are similar,
and *shǐ* (豕, 'pig') and *hài* (亥) are similar."
Upon arriving in Jìn and asking about it,
they said, "The Jìn army crossed the river on the *jǐ hài* day."
Words often resemble what is wrong yet seem right,
and often resemble what is right yet seem wrong.
The principles of right and wrong
must be distinguished.
This is what sages are cautious about.
So, how does one be cautious?
Understanding the feelings of things and the feelings of people and taking them as what you have heard, then you will obtain [understanding].
On Valuing Honesty, Part 3
23.1 "Valuing Honesty"
It says:
In dealing with people, one must certainly verify things with reason.
Lǔ Āigōng asked Kǒngzǐ, saying:
"I have heard that Yuèzhèng Kuí has one foot.
Is this true?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"In the past, Shùn wished to use music to spread teachings throughout the world.
He then ordered Chónglí to discover Kuí in the wilderness and recommend him.
Shùn appointed him as Yuèzhèng (music master).
Kuí then rectified the six lǜ (musical pitches),
harmonized the five shēng (musical notes),
and thus connected the eight winds,
and the world was greatly subdued.
Chónglí again wanted to seek out even more people.
Shùn said:
'Indeed, music is the essence of Heaven and Earth,
and the regulator of gain and loss.
Therefore, only a sage can harmonize the root of music.
Kuí is able to harmonize it,
and thereby pacify the world.
Someone like Kuí is enough.'
Therefore, it is said that Kuí has one foot,
but this does not mean he only has one foot."
In the state of Sòng, there was a Dīng family.
The family had no well and always went outside to irrigate and draw water.
One person was always outside doing this.
After the family dug a well,
they told people:
"By digging a well, we have obtained one person."
What a wise ruler values most is the scholar.
The reason for valuing scholars is
because they can speak frankly.
If words are frank, then what is crooked will be seen.
The worry of a ruler is that
he wants to hear what is crooked but hates frank words.
This is like blocking the source but wanting water,
from where will the water come?
It is devaluing what he desires and valuing what he hates,
from where will what he desires come?
Néng Yì met with King Xuān of Qí.
King Xuān said:
"I have heard that you, sir, love honesty,
is this so?"
He replied:
"How could Yì be honest?
Yì has heard that honest scholars
do not live in disordered countries,
and their persons do not appear before defiled rulers.
(My person now) Now, my person gets to see the king,
and my family dwells in Qí,
how could Yì be honest?"
Xuān Wáng 宣王, in anger, said:
"A rustic commoner!"
He was about to punish him.
Néng Yì 能意 said:
"When I was young, I loved good things;
when I grew up, I practiced them.
Why can't Your Majesty associate with rustic commoners?
Is it perhaps to make clear what he loves?"
The King then released him.
If someone like Néng Yì 能意 were made to carefully offer counsel by the ruler's side,
he would certainly not flatter the ruler.
If he does not flatter the ruler,
would what the ruler gains be little?
This is what a wise ruler seeks,
and what an unworthy ruler hates.
Hú Yuán 狐援 advised King Mǐn of Qí 齊湣王, saying:
"The tripods of Yīn 殷 are displayed in the court of Zhōu 周;
its altars are covered by the screens of Zhōu 周;
the sounds of its shields and axes
are amidst the people's entertainment.
The music of a destroyed state
is not allowed to reach the temple;
the altars of a destroyed state
are not allowed to be seen by Heaven;
the instruments of a destroyed state are displayed in the court,
in order to serve as a warning.
Your Majesty must strive!
"Do not let the great Lü bell of Qi be displayed in the court,
do not let the shrine of Grand Duke (Tàigōng) be covered by a screen,
do not let the music of Qi fill people's leisure."
The King of Qi did not accept this.
Hú Yuán came out and cried for the country for three days.
His words were:
"Those who left early
wore fine linen;
those who left late
filled the prisons.
Now I see the people wandering eastward, not knowing where to settle."
The King of Qi asked the officials, saying:
"What is the punishment for crying for the country?"
The official said:
"Beheading."
The King said:
"Carry out the law."
The official set out the axe and chopping block at the east gate,
not wanting to kill him,
but wanting to drive him away.
Hú Yuán heard this and stumbled towards it, passing by.
The official said:
"The punishment for crying for the country is beheading.
Is the Master old or confused?"
Hú Yuán said:
"Why confused?"
Thereupon he said:
"Someone is coming from the south,
fù rù ér ní jū,
causes the morning labors of the people to be for naught, and the state to become ruins.
Yīn had Bǐ Gān,
Wú had Zǐ Xū,
and Qí had Hú Yuán.
Already not using their words,
and then chopping them at the east gate.
Every chopper asks, "Am I comparable to those two gentlemen?"
Hú Yuán did not delight in being chopped;
the state was already in chaos,
the ruler was already perverse,
mourning for the state altars and the people,
therefore he uttered such words.
Uttering such words was not idle discourse,
but intended to rescue from ruin,
inherently bordering on danger.
This is why Chù Zǐ departed,
and Dá Zǐ died for it.
Zhào Jiǎn Zǐ attacked the outer walls of Wèi,
personally leading the troops.
When it came to battle,
he stood far back,
and moreover stayed under the cover of rhinoceros-hide shields and fortified towers.
He beat the drum, but the soldiers did not rise up.
Jiǎn Zǐ threw down the drumstick and sighed, saying:
"Alas!
Are the soldiers so exhausted and corrupt as this?"
Xíngrén Zhú Guò, with his helmet askew and spear held horizontally, advanced and said:
"Your servant has heard that
there are indeed times when the ruler is incapable,
what fault lies with the soldiers?"
Jiǎn Zǐ, with a look of displeasure, changed his expression and said:
"It is because I am not employing them well.
Now you, yourself, are leading this army.
You personally say that I am incapable.
If you have an explanation, then speak.
If you have no explanation, then you shall die."
He replied:
"In the past, five years after my former lord, Xiàn Gōng, ascended the throne,
he annexed nineteen states,
using these same soldiers.
Two years after Huì Gōng ascended the throne,
he indulged in lechery and became violently arrogant,
indulging himself in beautiful women.
The people of Qín attacked us,
retreating seventy *lǐ* from Jiàng,
using these same soldiers.
Two years after Wén Gōng ascended the throne,
he governed with courage.
Therefore, after three years, the soldiers were all bold and daring.
In the battle of Chéngpú,
he defeated the Jīng people five times.
He besieged Wèi, seized Cáo,
and captured Shíshè.
He secured the position of the Son of Heaven
To achieve a respected name throughout the world;
it is by using such men.
There are also rulers who cannot acquire them,
what fault is it of the men?"
Jiǎn Zǐ then removed the rhinoceros-hide screens and stood where arrows and stones could reach,
at the first drumbeat, the soldiers all mounted [the walls].
Jiǎn Zǐ said:
"Giving me a thousand war chariots,
is not as good as hearing a single word from the traveler Zhú Guò."
The traveler Zhú Guò can be said to be able to remonstrate with his ruler,
in the midst of battle,
as the drumsticks were about to be used,
without increasing rewards,
without increasing punishments,
with a single word, the soldiers were all happy to die for their superiors.
23.2 "Direct Admonition"
Secondly:
When words are extreme, [the ruler] becomes angry,
when angry, the speaker is in danger,
who but the wise would dare to risk danger?
But if they are not wise,
they will be seeking profit.
For those who seek profit,
what is the benefit of risking danger?
Therefore, unworthy rulers have no wise men.
Without wise men, they do not hear extreme words,
without hearing extreme words, then treacherous people form cliques, and all kinds of evils arise,
Ruò cǐ zé wú yǐ cún yǐ. If it is like this, then there is no way to survive.
Fán guó zhī cún yě, Generally speaking, the survival of a state,
zhǔ zhī ān yě, the peace of its ruler,
bì yǒu yǐ yě. must have a reason.
Bù zhī suǒ yǐ, If one does not know the reason,
suī cún bì wáng, even if it survives, it will surely perish;
suī ān bì wēi, even if it is at peace, it will surely be in danger.
Suǒ yǐ bùkě bù lùn yě. Therefore, the reasons cannot but be discussed.
Qí Huán Gōng, Guǎn Zhòng, Bào Shū, Níng Qī xiāng yǔ yǐn, Duke Huán of Qí, Guǎn Zhòng, Bào Shū, and Níng Qī were drinking together.
Jiǔ hān, As the wine flowed,
Huán Gōng wèi Bào Shū yuē: Duke Huán said to Bào Shū:
"Hé bù qǐ wèi guǎ rén shòu?" "Why not rise and offer a toast to me?"
Bào Shū fèng bēi ér jìn yuē: Bào Shū held the cup and stepped forward, saying:
"Shǐ gōng wú wàng chū bēn zài yú Jǔ yě, "May Your Grace not forget your exile in Jǔ;
shǐ Guǎn Zhòng wú wàng shù (zhuó) fù ér zài yú Lǔ yě, may Guǎn Zhòng not forget being bound and imprisoned in Lǔ;
shǐ Níng Qī wú wàng qí fàn niú ér jū yú chē xià." may Níng Qī not forget feeding cattle and living under the carriage."
Huán Gōng bì xí zài bài yuē: Duke Huán left his mat and bowed twice, saying:
"Guǎ rén yǔ dàfū néng jiē wú wàng fūzǐ zhī yán, "If I and my ministers can all not forget the words of you gentlemen,
zé Qí guó zhī shèjì xìng yú bù dài yǐ." then the altars of the Qí state will be fortunate enough to avoid danger."
Dāng cǐ shí yě, At that time,
Huán Gōng kě yǔ yán jí yán yǐ. Duke Huán could be spoken to with the most extreme words.
Kě yǔ yán jí yán, Because he could be spoken to with the most extreme words,
gù kě yǔ wéi bà. therefore he could become a Hegemon.
Jīng Wén Wáng dé Rú Huáng zhī gǒu, Wǎn Lù zhī zēng, King Wén of Jīng obtained a yellow dog from Rú and a Wǎn Lù crossbow,
yǐ tián yú Yún Mèng, and went hunting in Yún Mèng,
sān yuè bù fǎn; and did not return for three months.
dé Dān zhī jī, He obtained a beauty from Dān,
yín, and became licentious,
For a full year, he did not attend court.
Bǎo Shēn said:
"The late king divined, using me as a guardian,
and it was auspicious.
Now, the king has obtained a dog that resembles yellow, and the arrows of Wǎn Lù,
and hunts in Yún Mèng,
for three months without returning;
he has obtained a beauty from Dān,
and is licentious,
for a full year he does not attend court.
The king's offense deserves flogging."
The king said:
"I, the unworthy one, was spared from swaddling clothes and ranked among the feudal lords,
I wish to request a change and be spared the flogging."
Bǎo Shēn said:
"I have received the order of the late king,
and dare not abandon it.
If the king does not receive the flogging,
it is to abandon the late king's order.
I would rather offend the king,
than offend the late king."
The king said:
"Respectfully, I agree."
Then he pulled out a mat,
and the king prostrated himself.
Bǎo Shēn bound fifty thin whips,
knelt and applied them to the king's back,
and did this twice,
Someone told the king, "Rise, please."
The king said,
"To be flogged is a disgrace."
And so he had him brought forward.
Bǎo Shēn said,
"I have heard that gentlemen are shamed by it,
while commoners are pained by it.
If shame does not change him,
what good is the pain?"
Bǎo Shēn hastened to leave,
wanting to drown himself in the abyss,
and requested the death penalty.
Wén Wáng said,
"This is my fault.
What is Bǎo Shēn's crime?"
The king then changed his behavior,
summoned Bǎo Shēn,
killed the dog that ate yellow food,
broke the arrows from Wǎn Lù,
and released the Dān concubine.
Later, the state of Jīng annexed thirty-nine states.
That the state of Jīng became so large as it is today
is due to Bǎo Shēn's efforts and the merit of his candid speech.
23.3 "Knowing Transformation"
Thirdly,
those who serve others with courage do so with death in mind.
To speak of death before death,
is not considered;
To know or not to know when dead is the same.
In general, the value of wisdom
lies in knowing change.
Those rulers who are deluded are not like this.
When change has not arrived, they do not know it;
when change has arrived,
knowing it or not knowing it are one and the same.
Some things can be overlooked,
and some things cannot be overlooked.
But if it leads to personal death and national ruin,
how can that be overlooked?
This is what wise rulers value,
and what deluded rulers disregard.
What they disregard,
how can the state avoid danger?
How can the ruler avoid being in distress?
The path to danger and distress,
personal death and national ruin,
lies in not knowing change beforehand.
King Fūchāi of Wú is an example of this.
It's not that Zǐ Xū didn't know change beforehand,
but he advised and was not listened to,
therefore Wú became ruins,
and the disaster extended to Hélǘ.
King Fūchāi of Wú was about to attack Qí,
Zǐ Xū said:
"It is not permissible.
Qí and Wú,
Customs are different,
language is unintelligible,
if I obtain their land, I cannot settle there,

their language is intelligible,

Yuè is the same to me.

Yuè in relation to Wú,

Now, Qí in relation to Wú,
is like a scabies disease,

Now, to release Yuè and attack Qí,

even if one wins,

Grand Tutor Pǐ said:

The reason the King's commands are not implemented in the superior states
It's Qi and Jin.

Zǐxū, about to die, said:

Fūchā then took his body and floated it in the river,
They gouged out his eyes,

After several years,
Yue retaliated against Wu,

Fūchā, as he was about to die, said:
"If the dead have knowledge,

Thereupon, he made a mask to cover his face and died.
If calamity has not yet arrived,
then one cannot be warned;
once calamity has arrived,
even if one knows, it is too late.
Therefore, Fūchā's knowledge of his shame towards Zǐxū,
is not as good as not knowing.

Qín Mù Gōng 時 (During the time of Duke Mù of Qín),
Róng was strong.

Not hearing leads to the destruction of the ruler.

King Xuān's actual strength

Isn't that lamentable?
If not an upright scholar, who could avoid flattering the ruler?
Upright scholars in the world

Therefore, the trouble with the ruler of a disordered state

Discourse on Not Being Careless, Part Four
24.1 《Not Being Careless》
First:
The affair of the worthy,
though noble, they do not act carelessly,
Even though he listens, he does not comply for his own sake.
He only acts when it accords with principle.
He only initiates when it is appropriate for righteousness.
This is the conduct of a loyal minister.
It is what a virtuous ruler approves of.
Even though an unworthy ruler is unworthy, his approval
is not because he dislikes the sound of the words.
Even if a ruler is unworthy,
his approval of the words of a loyal minister is the same as that of a virtuous ruler,
but his actions in reality are different from those of a virtuous ruler.
Because of this difference, his achievements, reputation, disasters, and blessings are also different.
Because of this difference, Zǐ Xū was approved of by Hélǘ but disliked by Fūchāi.
Bǐ Gān was born and disliked by the Shāng dynasty, but after his death, he was approved of by the Zhōu dynasty.

Therefore, even the Son of Heaven can be overcome by humble commoners,

Now, the tiger was not someone who personally spoke of this matter,

Bào Shū 也。」

Sūn Shū'áo and Shěn Yǐn Jīng were friends.

There is no greater merit than recommending the worthy.
24.3 《Self-Knowledge》
It says in the third place:
If you want to know what is level and straight,
Then one must use plumb lines and compasses;
If one wishes to know squares and circles,
then one must use set squares and compasses;
If a ruler wishes to know himself,
then he must have upright officers.
Therefore, the Son of Heaven establishes assistants and advisors,
and appoints teachers and guardians,
in order to point out his faults.
Indeed, people are inherently unable to know themselves,
and the ruler is even more so.
Survival or ruin, safety or danger,
do not seek them from external sources,
the key lies in knowing oneself.
Yáo had a drum for inviting remonstrance,
Shùn had a board for slander,
Tāng had officers who directly pointed out his faults,
Wǔ Wáng had a small drum for warning and caution,
still they feared not being able to know themselves.
